Mathematics subject classification.

title: European Physical Society Grand Challenges Physics for Society in the Horizon 2050
creator: EPS Forum Physics, Society
description: Abstract Contributors Zeki Can Seskir Karlsruhe Institute of Technology - ITAS Karlstraße 11, 76133 Karlsruhe, Germany Jacob Biamonte Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology Bolshoy Boulevard 30, bld. 1, Moscow 121205, Russian Federation Chapter 1 Milestones of research activity in quantum computing Chapter Abstract We argue that quantum computing underwent an inflection point circa 2017.

title: Optimal design of compliant displacement magnification mechanisms using stress-constrained topology optimization based on effective energy Journal: Elsevier
creator: K. Miyajima, Y. Noguchi, T. Yamada
description: Abstract In this paper, stress-constrained topology optimization is applied to the design of compliant displacement magnification mechanisms. By formulating the objective function based on the concept of effective energy, it is not necessary to place artificial spring components at the boundaries of the output and input ports as in previous methods.

title: TENSOR NETWORKS IN MACHINE LEARNING
creator: Richik Sengupta, Soumik Adhikary, Ivan Oseledets, Jacob Biamonte
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Richik Sengupta, Soumik Adhikary, Ivan Oseledets, Jacob Biamonte. A tensor network is a type of decomposition used to express and approximate large arrays of data. A given data-set, quantum state or higher dimensional multi-linear map is factored and approximated by a composition of smaller multi-linear maps. This is reminiscent to how a Boolean function might be decomposed into a gate array: this represents a special case of tensor decomposition, in which the tensor entries are replaced by 0, 1 and the factorisation becomes exact.

title: Anomalous Dimensions from Soft Regge Constants Preprint: MIT–CTP 5448
creator: Ian Moult, Sanjay Raman, Gregory Ridgway, Iain W. Stewart
description: Abstract Using an effective field theory (EFT) formalism for forward scattering, we reconsider the factorization of 2 → 2 2\to 2 scattering amplitudes in the Regge limit. Expanding the amplitude in gauge invariant operators labelled by the number of Glauber exchanges, allows us to further factorize the standard impact factors into separate collinear and soft functions.

title: Verifying the Union of Manifolds Hypothesis for Image Data
creator: Bradley C.A. Brown, Anthony L. Caterini, Brendan Leigh Ross, Jesse C. Cresswell, Gabriel Loaiza-Ganem
description: Abstract Deep learning has had tremendous success at learning low-dimensional representations of high-dimensional data. This success would be impossible if there was no hidden low-dimensional structure in data of interest; this existence is posited by the manifold hypothesis , which states that the data lies on an unknown manifold of low intrinsic dimension.

title: Dynamics of Stellar Disk Tilting from Satellite Mergers 2022 Dynamics of Stellar Disk Tilting from Satellite Mergers – B1
creator: Benjamin C. Dodge, Oren Slone, Mariangela Lisanti, Timothy Cohen
description: Abstract The Milky Way’s stellar disk can tilt in response to torques that result from infalling satellite galaxies and their associated tidal debris. In this work, we explore the dynamics of disk tilting by running N N -body simulations of mergers in an isolated, isotropic Milky Way–like host galaxy, varying over satellite virial mass, initial position, and orbit.

title: A candidate relativistic tidal disruption event at 340 Mpc
creator: Jean J. Somalwar, Vikram Ravi, Dillon Z. Dong, Yuyang Chen, Shari Breen, Poonam Chandra, Tracy Clarke, Kishalay De, B. M. Gaensler, Gregg Hallinan, Sibasish Laha, Casey Law, Steven T. Myers, Tyler Parsotan, Wendy Peters, Emil Polisensky
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jean J. Somalwar, Vikram Ravi, Dillon Z. Dong, Yuyang Chen, Shari Breen, Poonam Chandra, Tracy Clarke, Kishalay De, B. M. Gaensler, Gregg Hallinan, Sibasish Laha, Casey Law, Steven T. Myers, Tyler Parsotan, Wendy Peters, Emil Polisensky. We present observations of an extreme radio flare, VT J024345.70-284040.08, hereafter VT J0243, from the nucleus of a galaxy with evidence for historic Seyfert activity at redshift z = 0.074 z=0.074 .

title: Monitored Quantum Dynamics and the Kitaev Spin Liquid
creator: Ali Lavasani, Zhu-Xi Luo, Sagar Vijay
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ali Lavasani, Zhu-Xi Luo, Sagar Vijay. Quantum circuit dynamics with local projective measurements can realize a rich spectrum of entangled states of quantum matter. Motivated by the physics of the Kitaev quantum spin liquid Kitaev 2006 , we study quantum circuit dynamics in (2+1)-dimensions involving local projective measurements, in which the monitored trajectories realize (i) a phase with topological quantum order or (ii) a “critical” phase with a logarithmic violation of area-law-scaling of the entanglement entropy along with long range tripartite entanglement.

title: Spectrum of the Hypereclectic Spin Chain and Pólya Counting
creator: Changrim Ahn, Matthias Staudacher
description: Abstract In earlier work we proposed a generating function that encodes the Jordan block spectrum of the integrable Hypereclectic spin chain, related to the one-loop dilatation operator of the dynamical fishnet quantum field theory. We significantly improve the expressions for these generating functions, rendering them much more explicit and elegant.

title: Scalar leptoquarks at the LHC and flavour anomalies: a comparison of pair-production modes at NLO-QCD Preprint: KIAS-Q22010, CTPU-PTC-22-24, CERN-TH-2022-106, KA-TP-17-2022, MS-TP-22-18
creator: Christoph Borschensky, ​​, Benjamin Fuks, ​​, Adil Jueid, ​ and Anna Kulesza
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Christoph Borschensky, ​​, Benjamin Fuks, ​​, Adil Jueid, ​ and Anna Kulesza. We analyse scalar leptoquark pair production at the LHC with predictions including t t -channel lepton exchange contributions up to next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD. In particular, we calculate NLO-QCD predictions for off-diagonal production channels, i.e.

title: Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods for graph refinement in Spinfoam Cosmology
creator: Francesca Vidotto
description: Abstract We study the behaviour of the Lorentzian Engle-Pereira-Rovelli-Livine spinfoam amplitude with homogeneous boundary data, under a graph refinement going from five to twenty boundary tetrahedra. This can be interpreted as a wave function of the universe, for which we compute boundary geometrical operators, correlation functions and entanglement entropy.

title: A handbook of holographic 4-point functions
creator: Adam Bzowski, Paul McFadden, and Kostas Skenderis
description: Abstract We present a comprehensive discussion of tree-level holographic 4 4 -point functions of scalar operators in momentum space. We show that each individual Witten diagram satisfies the conformal Ward identities on its own and is thus a valid conformal correlator.

title: Recursive Time Series Data Augmentation
creator: Amine Mohamed Aboussalah, Min-Jae Kwon, Raj G Patel, Cheng Chi, Chi-Guhn Lee
description: Abstract Time series observations can be seen as realizations of an underlying dynamical system governed by rules that we typically do not know. For time series learning tasks we create our model using available data. Training on available realizations, where data is limited, often induces severe over-fitting thereby preventing generalization.

title: Topological magnons on the triangular kagome lattice
creator: Meng-Han Zhang, Dao-Xin Yao
description: Abstract We present the topology of magnons on the triangular kagome lattice (TKL) by calculating its Berry curvature, Chern number and edge states. In addition to the ferromagnetic state, the TKL hosts ferrimagnetic ground state as its two sublattices can couple with each other either ferromagnetically or antiferromagnetically.

title: Pure circularly polarized light emission from waveguide microring resonators
creator: Leonardo Massai, Tom Schatteburg, Jonathan P. Home, Karan K. Mehta ∗
description: Abstract Circularly polarized light plays a key role in many applications including spectroscopy, microscopy, and control of atomic systems. Particularly in the latter, high polarization purity is often required. Integrated technologies for atomic control are progressing rapidly, but while integrated photonics can generate fields with pure linear polarization, integrated generation of highly pure circular polarization states has not been addressed.

title: Surface particle motions excited by a low velocity normal impact into a granular medium
creator: Max Neiderbach, Bingcheng Suo, Esteban Wright, A. C. Quillen, Mokin Lee, Peter Miklavcic, Hesam Askari, Paul Sánchez
description: Abstract In laboratory experiments, high speed videos are used to detect and track mm-size surface particle motions caused by a low velocity normal impact into sand. Outside the final crater radius and prior to the landing of the ejecta curtain, particle displacements are measured via particle tracking velocimetry and with a cross-correlation method.

title: Inter and Intra Signal Variance in Feature Extraction and Classification of Affective State Thanks: This publication has emanated from research supported in part by a Grant from Science Foundation Ireland under Grant number 18/CRT/6222
creator: Zachary Dair, Samantha Dockray, Ruairi O’Reilly
description: Abstract Psychophysiology investigates the causal relationship of physiological changes resulting from psychological states. There are significant challenges with machine learning-based momentary assessments of physiology due to varying data collection methods, physiological differences, data availability and the requirement for expertly annotated data.

title: A signature index for third order topological insulators
creator: L.B Drissi, E.H Saidi 1- LPHE, Modeling & Simulations, Faculty of Science, Mohammed V University, Rabat, Morocco.2- CPM, Centre of Physics and Mathematics, Mohammed V University in Rabat, Morocco.3- Peter Grünberg Institut and Institute for Advanced Simulation, Forschungszentrum Jülich & JARA, D-524
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by L.B Drissi, E.H Saidi 1- LPHE, Modeling & Simulations, Faculty of Science, Mohammed V University, Rabat, Morocco.2- CPM, Centre of Physics and Mathematics, Mohammed V University in Rabat, Morocco.3- Peter Grünberg Institut and Institute for Advanced Simulation, Forschungszentrum Jülich & JARA, D-524. In this work, we develop an index signature characterising the third order topological phases in 3D systems. This index is an alternating sum of monomial signatures of Higgs triplet values at 3D corners.

title: Private Information Acquisition and Preemption: a Strategic Wald Problem
creator: Guo Bai
description: Abstract This paper studies a dynamic information acquisition model with payoff externalities. Two players can acquire costly information about an unknown state before taking a safe or risky action. Both information and the action taken are private. The first player to take the risky action has an advantage but whether the risky action is profitable depends on the state.

title: On The Universality of Diagrams for Causal Inference and The Causal Reproducing Property
creator: Sridhar Mahadevan
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sridhar Mahadevan. Humans have sought to understand causality since ancient times. 2500 years ago, Plato remarked that "Everything that becomes or changes must do so owing to some cause; for nothing can come to be without a cause" . In more modern times, Judea Pearl developed a seminal theory of causality based on directed acyclic graph (DAG) models, where a variable X X has a causal influence on variable Y Y if a directed path exists between X X and Y Y .

title: Speckle Interferometry at SOAR in 2021
creator: Andrei Tokovinin, Brian D. Mason, Rene A. Mendez, Edgardo Costa
description: Abstract The speckle interferometry program at the the 4.1 m Southern Astrophysical Research Telescope (SOAR), started in 2008, now accumulated over 30,300 individual observations of 12,700 distinct targets. Its main goal is to monitor orbital motion of close binaries, including members of high-order hierarchies and low-mass dwarfs in the solar neighborhood.

title: The Variations of SIkJalpha Model for COVID-19 Forecasting and Scenario Projections
creator: Ajitesh Srivastava
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ajitesh Srivastava. We proposed the SIkJalpha model at the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic (early 2020). Since then, as the pandemic evolved, more complexities were added to capture crucial factors and variables that can assist with projecting desired future scenarios. Throughout the pandemic, multi-model collaborative efforts have been organized to predict short-term outcomes (cases, deaths, and hospitalizations) of COVID-19 and long-term scenario projections. We have been participating in five such efforts.

title: Electrically-driven Photonic Crystal Lasers with Ultra-low Threshold
creator: Evangelos Dimopoulos, Aurimas Sakanas, Andrey Marchevsky, Meng Xiong, Yi Yu, Elizaveta Semenova, Jesper Mørk, Kresten Yvind
description: Abstract Light sources with ultra-low energy consumption and high performance are required to realize optical interconnects for on-chip communication. Photonic crystal (PhC) nanocavity lasers are one of the most promising candidates to fill this role. In this work, we demonstrate an electrically-driven PhC nanolaser with an ultra-low threshold current of 10.

title: Learning Optimal Solutions via an LSTM-Optimization Framework
creator: Dogacan Yilmaz, İ. Esra Büyüktahtakın
description: Abstract In this study, we present a deep learning-optimization framework to tackle dynamic mixed-integer programs. Specifically, we develop a bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) framework that can process information forward and backward in time to learn optimal solutions to sequential decision-making problems.

title: Boosting the interpretability of clinical risk scores with intervention predictions DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: 2022 KDD Workshop on Applied Data Science for Healthcare; August 14–17, 2022; Washington DC 2022 KDD Workshop on Applied Data Science for Healthcare Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX
creator: Eric Loreaux, Ke Yu, Jonas Kemp, Martin Seneviratne, Christina Chen, Subhrajit Roy, Ivan Protsyuk, Natalie Harris, Alexander D’Amour, Steve Yadlowsky, Ming-Jun Chen
description: Abstract . Machine learning systems show significant promise for forecasting patient adverse events via risk scores. However, these risk scores implicitly encode assumptions about future interventions that the patient is likely to receive, based on the intervention policy present in the training data. Without this important context, predictions from such systems are less interpretable for clinicians.

title: Comprehensive Listing of 156 Reliable Orbital Periods for Novae, Including 49 New Periods 2021 Comprehensive Listing of 156 Reliable Orbital Periods for Novae, Including 49 New Periods – References
creator: Bradley E. Schaefer
description: Abstract I report on a large-scale search for the orbital periods ( P P ) of most known nova systems, by looking for significant, coherent, and stable optical photometric modulation in two or more independent light curves taken mostly from the large surveys of T ​ E ​ S ​ S TESS , K ​ e ​ p ​ l

title: New Analysis of Dark Matter in Elliptical Galaxies
creator: D. M. Winters 1 , A. Deur 1,2 , X. Zheng 1 1 University of Virginia, Charlottesville, Virginia 22904, USA 2 Old Dominion University, Norfolk, VA 23508, USA
description: Abstract We investigate a correlation between the dark matter content of elliptical galaxies and their ellipticity ϵ \epsilon that was initially reported in 2014. We use new determinations of dark matter and ellipticities that are posterior to that time. Our data set consists of 237 elliptical galaxies passing a strict set of criteria.

title: First-Photon Target Detection: Beating Nair’s Pure-Loss Performance Limit
creator: Jeffrey H. Shapiro
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jeffrey H. Shapiro. In 2011, Nair published a no-go theorem for quantum radar target detection [Phys. A 84 , 032312 (2011)]. He showed, under fairly general assumptions, that a coherent-state radar’s error probability was within a factor of two of the best possible quantum performance for the pure-loss (no background radiation) channel whose roundtrip radar-to-target-to-radar transmissivity κ \kappa satisfies κ ≪ 1 \kappa\ll 1 . We introduce first-photon radars (FPRs) to circumvent and beat Nair’s performance limit.

title: The use of Synthetic Data to solve the scalability and data availability problems in Smart City Digital Twins
creator: Esteve Almirall, Davide Callegaro, Peter Bruins, Mar Santamaría, Pablo Martrínez, Ulises Cortés
description: Abstract The A.I. disruption and the need to compete on innovation are impacting cities that have an increasing necessity to become innovation hotspots. However, without proven solutions, experimentation, often unsuccessful, is needed. But experimentation in cities has many undesirable effects not only for its citizens but also reputational if unsuccessful.

title: Cost-efficient Payoffs under Model Ambiguity Thanks: Institute of Mathematics, Carl von Ossietzky University, 26111 Oldenburg, Germany (e-mail: gero.junike@uol.de ). Thanks: Helvetia Insurance Group (e-mail: thibaut.lux@helvetia.ch ). Thanks: Steven Vanduffel, Department of Economics and Political S
creator: Carole Bernard
description: Abstract Dybvig 1988a ; Dybvig 1988b solves in a complete market setting the problem of finding a payoff that is cheapest possible in reaching a given target distribution (“cost-efficient payoff”). In the presence of ambiguity, the distribution of a payoff is, however, no longer known with certainty.

title: On the two-dimensional time-dependent anisotropic harmonic oscillator in a magnetic field
creator: Pinaki Patra
description: Abstract A Charged harmonic oscillator in a magnetic field, Landau problems, and an oscillator in a noncommutative space, share the same mathematical structure in their Hamiltonians. We have considered a two-dimensional anisotropic harmonic oscillator (AHO) with arbitrarily time-dependent parameters (effective mass and frequencies), placed in an arbitrarily time-dependent magnetic field.

title: Context-aware Self-supervised Learning for Medical Images Using Graph Neural Network
creator: Li Sun, Ke Yu, Kayhan BatmanghelichUniversity of Pittsburgh, USA {lis118, key44, kayhan}@pitt.edu
description: Abstract Although self-supervised learning enables us to bootstrap the training by exploiting unlabeled data, the generic self-supervised methods for natural images do not sufficiently incorporate the context . For medical images, a desirable method should be sensitive enough to detect deviation from normal-appearing tissue of each anatomical region; here, anatomy is the context.
