title: Search for dark matter-nucleon interactions via Migdal effect with DarkSide-50
creator: P. Agnes, I.F.M. Albuquerque, T. Alexander, A.K. Alton, M. Ave, H.O. Back, G. Batignani, K. Biery, V. Bocci, W.M. Bonivento, B. Bottino, S. Bussino, M. Cadeddu, M. Cadoni, F. Calaprice, A. Caminata, M.D. Campos, N. Canci, M. Caravati, N. Cargioli, M. Cariello, M. Carlini, V. Cataudella, P. Cavalcant
description: Abstract Dark matter elastic scattering off nuclei can result in the excitation and ionization of the recoiling atom through the so-called Migdal effect. The energy deposition from the ionization electron adds to the energy deposited by the recoiling nuclear system and allows for the detection of interactions of sub-GeV/c 2 mass dark matter.

title: Search for low-mass dark matter WIMPs with 12 ton-day exposure of DarkSide-50
creator: P. Agnes, I.F.M. Albuquerque, T. Alexander, A.K. Alton, M. Ave, H.O. Back, G. Batignani, K. Biery, V. Bocci, W.M. Bonivento, B. Bottino, S. Bussino, M. Cadeddu, M. Cadoni, F. Calaprice, A. title: Semiparametric Estimation on Multi-treatment Causal Effects via Cross-Fitting
creator: Jingying Zeng
description: Abstract Causal inference is a critical research area with multi-disciplinary origins and applications, ranging from statistics, computer science, economics, psychology to public health. In many scientific research, randomized experiments provide a golden standard for estimation of causal effects for decades.

title: Search for dark matter particle interactions with electron final states with DarkSide-50
creator: P. Agnes, I.F.M. Albuquerque, T. Alexander, A.K. Alton, M. Ave, H.O. Back, G. Batignani, K. Biery, V. Bocci, W.M. Bonivento, B. Bottino, S. Bussino, M. Cadeddu, M. Cadoni, F. Calaprice, A. Caminata, M.D. Campos, N. Canci, M. Caravati, N. Cargioli, M. Cariello, M. Carlini, V. Cataudella, P. Cavalcant

Cadeddu, M. Cadoni, F. Calaprice, A. Caminata, M.D. Campos, N. Canci, M. Caravati, N. Cargioli, M. Cariello, M. Carlini, V. Cataudella, P. Cavalcant.

title: Existence of planar non-symmetric stationary flows with large flux in an exterior disk
creator: Mitsuo Higaki
description: Abstract Abstract. This paper is concerned with the two-dimensional stationary Navier-Stokes system in the domain exterior to the unit disk. The existence of solutions with critical decay O(|x|^{-1}) is established around some explicit flows with large flux. The solutions are obtained for non-symmetric external forces, and moreover, are unique in a certain class.

title: Large Room Temperature Bulk DNP of 13 C via P1 Centers in Diamond
creator: Daphna Shimon, Kelly A. Cantwell, Linta Joseph, Ethan Q. Williams, Zaili Peng, Susumu Takahashi, Chandrasekhar Ramanathan
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Daphna Shimon, Kelly A. Cantwell, Linta Joseph, Ethan Q. Williams, Zaili Peng, Susumu Takahashi, Chandrasekhar Ramanathan. We use microwave-induced dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP) of the substitutional nitrogen defects (P1 centers) in diamond to hyperpolarize bulk 13 C nuclei in both single crystal and powder samples at room temperature at 3.34 T. The large ( > 100 >100 -fold) enhancements demonstrated correspond to a greater than 10,000 fold improvement in terms of signal averaging of the 1% abundant 13 C spins.

title: Comment on ”Nanoscale Wetting of Crystalline Cellulose”
creator: David C. Malaspina, Jordi Faraudo
description: Abstract In a recent publication, Trentin et al. Trentin et al. 2021 employed Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations for the theoretical study of the wetting of the different polymorphs of cellulose by water, using the widely employed TIP3P model of water.

title: Power Flows with Flat Voltage Profiles: an Exact Approach
creator: Anthony B. Morton
description: Abstract 1 Background: the DC Power Flow conditions Analysis of alternating–current electrical networks with prescribed power flows is complicated by the fact that network quantities are defined by two degrees of freedom, amplitude and phase displacement. This greatly complicates the mathematics compared with that of DC circuits and of AC circuits with prescribed currents.

title: How does gravity influence freezing dynamics of drops on a solid surface
creator: Hao Zeng, Sijia Lyu, Dominique Legendre, Chao Sun
description: Abstract Water droplet freezing is a common phenomenon in our daily life. In both natural scenarios and industrial production, different surface inclinations bring distinctive deformation and freezing dynamics to frozen droplets. We explore the freezing of pendent and sessile droplets at different Bond number regimes.

title: Onset of Quantum Chaos in Random Field Theories
creator: Micha Berkooz, Adar Sharon, Navot Silberstein, Erez Y. Urbach
description: Abstract We study the quantum Lyapunov exponent λ L \lambda_{L} in theories with spacetime-independent disorder. We first derive self-consistency equations for the two- and four-point functions for products of N N models coupled by disorder at large N N , generalizing the equations appearing in SYK-like models.

title: Deep dual stream residual network with contextual attention for pansharpening of remote sensing images
creator: Syeda Roshana Ali, Anis U. Rahman, Muhammad Shahzad
description: Abstract Pansharpening enhances spatial details of high spectral resolution multispectral images using features of high spatial resolution panchromatic image. There are a number of traditional pansharpening approaches but producing an image exhibiting high spectral and spatial fidelity is still an open problem.

title: TransCL: Transformer Makes Strong and Flexible Compressive Learning
creator: Chong Mou, Jian Zhang
description: Abstract Compressive learning (CL) is an emerging framework that integrates signal acquisition via compressed sensing (CS) and machine learning for inference tasks directly on a small number of measurements. It can be a promising alternative to classical image-domain methods and enjoys great advantages in memory saving and computational efficiency.

title: Observer Design for the State Estimation of Epidemic Processes
creator: Muhammad Umar B. Niazi, Karl Henrik Johansson
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Muhammad Umar B. Niazi, Karl Henrik Johansson. Although an appropriate choice of measured state variables may ensure observability, designing state observers for the state estimation of epidemic models remains a challenging task. Epidemic spread is a nonlinear process, often modeled as the law of mass action, which is of a quadratic form; thus, on a compact domain, its Lipschitz constant turns out to be local and relatively large, which renders the Lipschitz-based design criteria of existing observer architectures infeasible.

title: Good Locally Testable Codes
creator: Irit Dinur, Shai Evra, Ron Livne, Alexander Lubotzky, Shahar Mozes
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Irit Dinur, Shai Evra, Ron Livne, Alexander Lubotzky, Shahar Mozes. An explicit construction of locally testable codes of constant rate, constant distance and constant number of queries is given. Hence answering affirmatively the c 3 c^{3} -problem. 1 Introduction An [n,k,d] binary linear error correcting code is a subspace C of \mathbb{F}_{2}^{n} , of dimension k=\dim C , and distance d=\min\{\mbox{wt}(c)\,:\,0\neq c\in C\} , where \mbox{wt}(c)=|\{1\leq i\leq n\,|\,c_{i}\neq 0\}| is the Hamming weight.

title: Geometric T-duality: Buscher rules in general topology
creator: Konrad Waldorf
description: Abstract The classical Buscher rules describe T-duality for metrics and B-fields in a topologically trivial setting. On the other hand, topological T-duality addresses aspects of non-trivial topology while neglecting metrics and B-fields. In this article we develop a new unifying framework for both aspects.

title: LETS-GZSL: A Latent Embedding Model for Time Series Generalized Zero Shot Learning
creator: Sathvik Bhaskarpandit, Priyanka Gupta, Manik Gupta
description: Abstract One of the recent developments in deep learning is generalized zero-shot learning (GZSL), which aims to recognize objects from both seen and unseen classes, when only the labeled examples from seen classes are provided. Over the past couple of years, GZSL has picked up traction and several models have been proposed to solve this problem.

title: Machine-checked executable semantics of Stateflow
creator: Shicheng Yi, Shuling Wang, Bohua Zhan, Naijun Zhan
description: Abstract Simulink is a widely used model-based development environment for embedded systems. Stateflow is a component of Simulink for modeling event-driven control via hierarchical state machines and flow charts. However, Stateflow lacks an official formal semantics, making it difficult to formally prove properties of its models in safety-critical applications.

title: GNN Transformation Framework for Improving Efficiency and Scalability
creator: Seiji Maekawa ✉, Yuya Sasaki, George Fletcher, Makoto Onizuka
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Seiji Maekawa ✉, Yuya Sasaki, George Fletcher, Makoto Onizuka. We propose a framework that automatically transforms non-scalable GNNs into precomputation-based GNNs which are efficient and scalable for large-scale graphs. The advantages of our framework are two-fold; 1) it transforms various non-scalable GNNs to scale well to large-scale graphs by separating local feature aggregation from weight learning in their graph convolution, 2) it efficiently executes precomputation on GPU for large-scale graphs by decomposing their edges into small disjoint and balanced sets.

title: Calculating Concentratable Entanglement in Graph States
creator: Alice R. Cullen, Pieter Kok
description:
A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alice R. Cullen, Pieter Kok. We propose a method to calculate the purity of reduced states of graph states entirely within the stabilizer formalism, using only the stabilizer generators for a given state. We apply this method to find the Concentratable Entanglement of graph states, with examples including a single qubit within any graph state, states proposed for use in quantum repeaters and states that maximise and minimise the overall Concentratable Entanglement. title: Graphene Dirac fermions in symmetric electric and magnetic fields: the case of an electric square well
creator: İsmail Burak Ateş, Şengül Kuru, Javier Negro
description: Abstract In this paper, a simple method is proposed to get analytical solutions (or with the help of a finite numerical calculations) of the Dirac-Weyl equation for low energy electrons in graphene in the presence of certain electric and magnetic fields.

title: Domain-invariant Feature Exploration for Domain Generalization
creator: Wang Lu luwang@ict.ac.cn, Jindong Wang jindong.wang@microsoft.com, Haoliang Li haoliang.li@cityu.edu.hk, Yiqiang Chen yqchen@ict.ac.cn, Xing Xie xingx@microsoft.com
description: Abstract Deep learning has achieved great success in the past few years. However, the performance of deep learning is likely to impede in face of non-IID situations. Domain generalization (DG) enables a model to generalize to an unseen test distribution, i.e., to learn domain-invariant representations.

title: Neural Generation Meets Real People: Building a Social, Informative Open-Domain Dialogue Agent
creator: Ethan A. Chi, Ashwin Paranjape, Abigail See, Caleb Chiam, Trenton Chang Kathleen Kenealy, Swee Kiat Lim, Amelia Hardy, Chetanya Rastogi, Haojun Li,Alexander Iyabor, Yutong He, Hari Sowrirajan, Peng Qi, Kaushik Ram Sadagopan,Nguyet Minh Phu, Dilara Soylu, Jillian Tang, Avanika Narayan,Giovanni Campag
description: Abstract We present Chirpy Cardinal, an open-domain social chatbot. Aiming to be both informative and conversational, our bot chats with users in an authentic, emotionally intelligent way. By integrating controlled neural generation with scaffolded, hand-written dialogue, we let both the user and bot take turns driving the conversation, producing an engaging and socially fluent experience.

title: Contrastive Learning for Interactive Recommendation in Fashion Conference: Make sure to enter the correct; July 15 2022; Madrid - Spain Conference: ACM SIGIR Workshop on eCommerce; July 15, 2022; Madrid, Spain
creator: Karin Sevegnani, Arjun Seshadri, Tian Wang, Anurag Beniwal, Julian McAuley, Alan Lu, Gerard Medioni
description: Abstract . Recommender systems and search are both indispensable in facilitating personalization and ease of browsing in online fashion platforms. However, the two tools often operate independently, failing to combine the strengths of recommender systems to accurately capture user tastes with search systems’ ability to process user queries.

title: Hilbert Complexes with Mixed Boundary Conditions Part 3: Biharmonic Complexes Thanks: Acknowledgements.
