description: Abstract In this Letter we demonstrate that a future accelerator-based neutrino experiment such as DUNE can greatly increase its sensitivity to a variety of new physics scenarios by operating in a mode where the proton beam impinges on a beam dump.

title: Dust Grain Growth & Dusty Supernovae in Low-Metallicity Molecular Clouds Note: Accepted by ApJ: June 11th, 2022.
creator: Sergio Martínez-González, Richard Wünsch, Guillermo Tenorio-Tagle, Sergiy Silich, Dorottya Szécsi, Jan Palouš
description: Abstract We present 3-D hydrodynamical models of the evolution of superbubbles powered by stellar winds and supernovae from young coeval massive star clusters within low metallicity ( Z = 0.02 ​ Z ⊙ Z=0.02\,\thinspace\hbox{$\hbox{Z}_{\odot}$} ), clumpy molecular clouds. We explore the initial stages of the superbubble evolution, including the occurrence of pair-instability and core-collapse supernovae.

title: Null states from large superpositions of two-sided black holes
creator: John Gardiner
description: Abstract A standard insight of the AdS/CFT correspondence is that some aspects of the geometry of a bulk state are encoded in the entanglement structure of its dual boundary state. As entanglement is not a linear quantum observable, this means that geometry in a quantum theory of gravity should likewise not be a linear observable.

title: Spectrahedral Shadows and Completely Positive Maps on Real Closed Fields Thanks: Manuel Bodirsky received funding from the ERC under the European Community’s Seventh Framework Programme (Grant Agreement no. 681988, CSP-Infinity). Mario Kummer was partially supported by DFG grant 421473641. Andreas T
creator: Manuel Bodirsky, Mario Kummer, Andreas Thom
description: Abstract . In this article we develop new methods for exhibiting convex semialgebraic sets that are not spectrahedral shadows. We characterize when the set of nonnegative polynomials with a given support is a spectrahedral shadow in terms of sums of squares.

title: Jets from SANE Super-Eddington Accretion Disks: Morphology, Spectra, and Their Potential as Targets for ngEHT 2022 Jets from SANE Super-Eddington Accretion Disks: Morphology, Spectra, and Their Potential as Targets for ngEHT – 25
creator: Brandon Curd, Razieh Emami, Richard Anantua, Daniel Palumbo, Sheperd Doeleman, Ramesh Narayan
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Brandon Curd, Razieh Emami, Richard Anantua, Daniel Palumbo, Sheperd Doeleman, Ramesh Narayan. We present general relativistic radiation magnetohydrodynamics (GRRMHD) simulations of super-Eddington accretion flows around supermassive black holes (SMBHs) which may apply to tidal disruption events (TDEs). We perform long duration ( t ≥ 81,200 ​ G ​ M / c 3 t\geq 81,200\,GM/c^{3} ) simulations which achieve mass accretion rates ≳ 11 \gtrsim 11 times the Eddington rate and produce thermal synchrotron spectra and images of their jets.

title: The Lyman Alpha Reference Sample XIII: High-Angular Resolution 21cm HI observations of Ly α {\alpha} emitting galaxies Journal: ApJ Facilities: VLA, HST(ACS,COS), VLT:Yepun(MUSE), PMAS, IRAM:NOEMA, SMA, ALMA Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , casa ( M
creator: Alexandra Le Reste, Matthew Hayes, John M. Cannon, Edmund Christian Herenz, Jens Melinder, Veronica Menacho, Göran Östlin, Johannes Puschnig, T. Emil Rivera-Thorsen, Daniel Kunth, Nick Velikonja
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alexandra Le Reste, Matthew Hayes, John M. Cannon, Edmund Christian Herenz, Jens Melinder, Veronica Menacho, Göran Östlin, Johannes Puschnig, T. Emil Rivera-Thorsen, Daniel Kunth, Nick Velikonja. The Ly α {\alpha} emission line is one of the main observables of galaxies at high redshift, but its output depends strongly on the neutral gas distribution and kinematics around the star-forming regions where UV photons are produced.

title: On the eigenvalues of operators with gaps. Application to Dirac operators. Volume: xxxxxx
creator: Jean Dolbeault, Maria J. Esteban and Eric Séré
description: Abstract This paper is devoted to a general min-max characterization of the eigenvalues in a gap of the essential spectrum of a self-adjoint unbounded operator. We prove an abstract theorem, then we apply it to the case of Dirac operators with a Coulomb-like potential. The result is optimal for the Coulomb potential.

title: An iterative quantum-phase-estimation protocol for near-term quantum hardware
creator: Joseph G. Smith 1,2, Crispin H. W. Barnes 1, David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur 2
description: Abstract Given N tot N_{\textrm{tot}} applications of a unitary operation with an unknown phase θ \theta , a large-scale fault-tolerant quantum system can reduce an estimate’s error scaling from 𝒪 ⁡ [ 1 / N tot ] \mathcal{O}\left[1/\sqrt{N_{\textrm{tot}}}\right] to 𝒪 ⁡ [ 1 / N tot ] \mathcal{O}\left[1/{N_{\textrm{tot}}}\right] .

title: Accretion History of AGN: Estimating the Host Galaxy Properties in X-ray Luminous AGN from z=0-3
creator: Brandon Coleman, Allison Kirkpatrick, Kevin C. Cooke, Eilat Glikman, Stephanie La Massa, Stefano Marchesi, Alessandro Peca, Ezequiel Treister, Connor Auge, C. Megan Urry, Dave Sanders, Tracey Jane Turner, Tonima Tasnim Ananna
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Brandon Coleman, Allison Kirkpatrick, Kevin C. Cooke, Eilat Glikman, Stephanie La Massa, Stefano Marchesi, Alessandro Peca, Ezequiel Treister, Connor Auge, C. Megan Urry, Dave Sanders, Tracey Jane Turner, Tonima Tasnim Ananna. We aim to determine the intrinsic far-Infrared (far-IR) emission of X-ray-luminous quasars over cosmic time.

title: Observing nulling of primordial correlations via the 21 ​ cm 21\,\mathrm{cm} signal
creator: Shyam Balaji, H. V. Ragavendra, Shiv K. Sethi, Joseph Silk, L. Sriramkumar
description: Abstract The 21 ​ cm 21\,\mathrm{cm} line emitted by neutral hydrogen (HI) during the Dark Ages carries imprints of pristine primordial correlations. In models of inflation driven by a single, canonical scalar field, we show that a phase of ultra-slow-roll can lead to a null in all the primordial correlations at a specific wavenumber k dip k_{\mathrm{dip}} .

title: Existence and uniqueness of fixed point on closed ball in multiplicative
creator: 𝐆
description: Abstract Abstract In this article, we investigate some fixed point results satisfying a new generalized \Delta -implicit contractive condition in ordered complete multiplicative \mathbf{G}_{\mathcal{M}}- metric space. Also, some new definitions and fixed point theorems are presented in ordered complete multiplicative \mathbf{G}_{\mathcal{M}}- metric space. Furthermore, some nontrivial and illustrative examples are given to validate our obtained results.

title: Marginally Stable Current Sheets in Collisionless Magnetic Reconnection
creator: C. Granier, D. Borgogno, L. Comisso, D. Grasso, E. Tassi, R. Numata
description: Abstract Non-collisional current sheets that form during the nonlinear development of magnetic reconnection are characterized by a small thickness, of the order of the electron skin depth. They can become unstable to the formation of plasmoids, which allows the magnetic reconnection process to reach high reconnection rates.

title: (Un)boundedness of directional maximal operators through a notion of “Perron capacity” and an application
creator: Emma D’Aniello, Anthony Gauvan, Laurent Moonens
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Emma D’Aniello, Anthony Gauvan, Laurent Moonens. We introduce the notion of Perron capacity of a set of slopes Ω ⊂ ℝ \Omega\subset\mathbb{R} . Precisely, we prove that if the Perron capacity of Ω \Omega is finite then the directional maximal operator associated M Ω M_{\Omega} is not bounded on L p ​ ( ℝ 2 ) L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{2}) for any 1 < p < ∞ 1<p<\infty .

title: Proton and neutron exchange as a prelude to fusion at near-barrier energies
creator: J. E. Johnstone, Varinderjit Singh, R. Giri, S. Hudan, J. Vadas, R. T. deSouza, D. Ackermann, A. Chbihi, Q. Hourdille, A. Abbott, C. Balhoff, A. Hannaman, A. B. McIntosh, M. Sorensen, Z. Tobin, A. Wakhle, S. J. Yennello, M. A. Famiano, K. W. Brown, C. Santamaria, J. Lubian, H. O. Soler, B. V. Carlso
description: Abstract Systematic examination of fusion for 39,41,45,47 K + 28 Si and 36,44 Ar + 28 Si provides insight into the impact of neutron and proton exchange on fusion for nuclei at and near the N=20 and N=28 shells. Comparison of the reduced excitation functions reveals a marked difference between the behavior of open-shell and closed-shell systems.

title: Characterization of variational quantum algorithms using free fermions
creator: Gabriel Matos, Chris N. Self, Zlatko Papić, Konstantinos Meichanetzidis, Henrik Dreyer
description: Abstract We study variational quantum algorithms from the perspective of free fermions. By deriving the explicit structure of the associated Lie algebras, we show that the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) on a one-dimensional lattice – with and without decoupled angles – is able to prepare all fermionic Gaussian states respecting the symmetries of the circuit.

title: An A 5 A_{5} inverse seesaw model with perturbed golden ratio mixing
creator: A. E. Cárcamo Hernández a,b,c, Ivo de Medeiros Varzielas
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by A. E. Cárcamo Hernández a,b,c, Ivo de Medeiros Varzielas. We propose a theory based on the A 5 A_{5} discrete group which successfully accounts for lepton masses and mixings. In the proposed model, the neutrino masses arise from an inverse seesaw mechanism. The leptonic mixing consists in a perturbed golden ratio mixing pattern with a strong correlation arising between the leptonic mixing observables, which can be expressed as θ 13 \theta_{13} predicting the other mixing angles and the Dirac CP phase.

title: Projective characterization of higher-order quantum transformations
creator: Timothée Hoffreumon, Ognyan Oreshkov
description: Abstract Transformations of transformations, also called higher-order transformations, is a natural concept in information processing, which has recently attracted significant interest in the study of quantum causal relations. In this work, a framework for characterizing higher-order quantum transformations which relies on the use of superoperator projectors is presented.

title: Spin-driven jet feedback in idealised simulations of galaxy groups and clusters 2022 1–23
creator: Filip Huško, Cedric G. Lacey, Joop Schaye, Matthieu Schaller, Folkert S.J. Nobels
description: Abstract We implement a black hole spin evolution and jet feedback model into SWIFT, a smoothed particle hydrodynamics code. The jet power is determined self-consistently assuming that the black hole accretion rate is equal to the Bondi rate (i.e. the accretion efficiency is 100 % 100\% ), and using a realistic, spin-dependent efficiency.

title: Skylight : a new code for general-relativistic ray tracing and radiative transfer in arbitrary spacetimes
creator: Joaquín Pelle, Oscar Reula, Federico Carrasco, Carlos Bederian
description: Abstract To reproduce the observed spectra and light curves originated in the neighborhood of compact objects requires accurate relativistic ray-tracing codes. In this work we present Skylight , a new numerical code for general-relativistic ray tracing and radiative transfer in arbitrary space-time geometries and coordinate systems.

title: Dispersive Shock Waves in Lattices: A Dimension Reduction Approach
creator: Christopher Chong, Michael Herrmann, P. G. Kevrekidis
description: Abstract Dispersive shock waves (DSWs), which connect states of different amplitude via a modulated wave train, form generically in nonlinear dispersive media subjected to abrupt changes in state. The primary tool for the analytical study of DSWs is Whitham’s modulation theory.

title: Distribution of Quantum Circuits Over General Quantum Networks
creator: Ranjani G. Sundaram, Himanshu Gupta, C. R. Ramakrishnan
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ranjani G. Sundaram, Himanshu Gupta, C. R. Ramakrishnan. Near-term quantum computers can hold only a small number of qubits. One way to facilitate large-scale quantum computations is through a distributed network of quantum computers. In this work, we consider the problem of distributing quantum programs represented as quantum circuits across a quantum network of heterogeneous quantum computers, in a way that minimizes the overall communication cost required to execute the distributed circuit.

title: Symbolic Regression in Materials Science: Discovering Interatomic Potentials from Data
creator: Bogdan Burlacu, Michael Kommenda, Gabriel Kronberger, Stephan Winkler, Michael Affenzeller
description: Abstract Particle-based modeling of materials at atomic scale plays an important role in the development of new materials and understanding of their properties. The accuracy of particle simulations is determined by interatomic potentials , which allow to calculate the potential energy of an atomic system as a function of atomic coordinates and potentially other properties.

title: Proposed energy-metabolisms cannot explain the atmospheric chemistry of Venus
creator: Sean Jordan* 1, Oliver Shorttle 1,2, Paul B. Rimmer 2,3,4
description: Abstract . Life in the clouds of Venus, if present in sufficiently high abundance, must be affecting the atmospheric chemistry. It has been proposed that abundant Venusian life could obtain energy from its environment using three possible sulfur energy-metabolisms. These metabolisms raise the possibility of Venus’s enigmatic cloud-layer SO 2 \text{SO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} -depletion being caused by life.

title: Fitting Segmentation Networks on Varying Image Resolutions using Splatting
creator: Mikael Brudfors, Yaël Balbastre, John Ashburner, Geraint Rees, Parashkev Nachev, Sébastien Ourselin, M. Jorge Cardoso
description: Abstract Data used in image segmentation are not always defined on the same grid. This is particularly true for medical images, where the resolution, field-of-view and orientation can differ across channels and subjects. Images and labels are therefore commonly resampled onto the same grid, as a pre-processing step.

title: Differentiable and Transportable Structure Learning
creator: Jeroen Berrevoets, Nabeel Seedat, Fergus Imrie, Mihaela van der Schaar
description: Abstract Directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) encode a lot of information about a particular distribution in their structure. However, compute required to infer these structures is typically super-exponential in the number of variables, as inference requires a sweep of a combinatorially large space of potential structures.

title: Stable anisotropic minimal hypersurfaces in 𝐑 4 \mathbf{R}^{4}
creator: Otis Chodosh, Chao Li
description: Abstract . We show that a complete, two-sided, stable immersed anisotropic minimal hypersurface in 𝐑 4 \mathbf{R}^{4} has intrinsic cubic volume growth, provided the parametric elliptic integral is C 2 C^{2} -close to the area functional. We also obtain an interior volume upper bound for stable anisotropic minimal hypersurfaces in the unit ball.

title: A Dilemma for Solomonoff Prediction
creator: Sven Neth
description: Abstract The framework of Solomonoff prediction assigns prior probability to hypotheses inversely proportional to their Kolmogorov complexity. There are two well-known problems. First, the Solomonoff prior is relative to a choice of Universal Turing machine. Second, the Solomonoff prior is not computable. However, there are responses to both problems. Different Solomonoff priors converge with more and more data.

title: Mapping fNIRS to fMRI with Neural Data Augmentation and Machine Learning Models
creator: Jihyun Hur, Jaeyeong Yang, Hoyoung Doh, Woo-Young Ahn
description: Abstract Advances in neuroimaging techniques have provided us novel insights into understanding how the human mind works. Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) is the most popular and widely used neuroimaging technique, and there is growing interest in fMRI-based markers of individual differences.

title: A comparison of partial information decompositions using data from real and simulated layer 5b pyramidal cells
creator: Jim W. Kay, Jan M. Schulz, William A. Phillips
description: Abstract Partial information decomposition allows the joint mutual information between an output and a set of inputs to be divided into components that are synergistic or shared or unique to each input. We consider five different decompositions and compare their results on data from layer 5b pyramidal cells in two different studies.

title: Learning Task-Independent Game State Representations from Unlabeled Images Thanks: This project has received funding from the EU’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreements No 951911 and No 101003397.
creator: Chintan Trivedi, Konstantinos Makantasis, Antonios Liapis and Georgios N. Yannakakis
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Chintan Trivedi, Konstantinos Makantasis, Antonios Liapis and Georgios N. Yannakakis. Self-supervised learning (SSL) techniques have been widely used to learn compact and informative representations from high-dimensional complex data. In many computer vision tasks, such as image classification, such methods achieve state-of-the-art results that surpass supervised learning approaches. In this paper, we investigate whether SSL methods can be leveraged for the task of learning accurate state representations of games, and if so, to what extent.

title: Trimer covers in the triangular grid:
creator: twenty mostly open problems
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by twenty mostly open problems. In the past three decades, the study of rhombus tilings and domino tilings of various plane regions has been a thriving subfield of enumerative combinatorics. Physicists classify such work as the study of dimer covers of finite graphs.

title: RigNeRF: Fully Controllable Neural 3D Portraits
creator: ShahRukh Athar*, Zexiang Xu, Kalyan Sunkavalli, Eli Shechtman, Zhixin Shu
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by ShahRukh Athar*, Zexiang Xu, Kalyan Sunkavalli, Eli Shechtman, Zhixin Shu. Volumetric neural rendering methods, such as neural radiance fields (NeRFs), have enabled photo-realistic novel view synthesis. However, in their standard form, NeRFs do not support the editing of objects, such as a human head, within a scene. In this work, we propose RigNeRF, a system that goes beyond just novel view synthesis and enables full control of head pose and facial expressions learned from a single portrait video.

title: On several properties of uniformly optimal search plans
creator: Liang Hong
description: Abstract The uniformly optimal search plan is a cornerstone of the optimal search theory. It is well-known that when the target distribution is circular normal and the detection function is exponential, the uniformly search plan has several desirable properties. This article establishes that these properties hold for any continuous target distribution.

title: Chameleon Screening in Cosmic Voids
creator: and Thomas Vincent
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by and Thomas Vincent. A key goal in cosmology in the upcoming decade will be to form a better understanding of the accelerated expansion of the Universe. Upcoming surveys, such as the Vera C. Rubin Observatory’s 10-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), Euclid and the Square Killometer Array (SKA) will deliver key datasets required to tackle this and other puzzles in contemporary cosmology. With this data, constraints of unprecedented power will be put on different models of dark energy and modified gravity.

title: Activity gradients in two- and three-dimensional active nematics
creator: Liam J. Ruske, Julia M. Yeomans
description: Abstract We numerically investigate how spatial variations of extensile or contractile active stress affect bulk active nematic systems in two and three dimensions. In the absence of defects, activity gradients drive flows which re-orient the nematic director field and thus act as an effective anchoring force.

title: SN 2019zrk, a bright SN 2009ip analog with a precursor Thanks: Table 1 is only available in electronic form at the CDS via anonymous ftp to cdsarc.u-strasbg.fr (130.79.128.5) or via http://cdsweb.u-strasbg.fr/cgi-bin/qcat?J/A+A/
creator: Claes Fransson, Jesper Sollerman, Nora L. Strotjohann, Sheng Yang, Steve Schulze, Cristina Barbarino, Erik C. Kool, Eran O. Ofek, Arien Crellin-Quick, Kishalay De, Andrew J. Drake, Christoffer Fremling, Avishay Gal-Yam, Anna Y. Q. Ho, Mansi M. Kasliwal
description: Abstract We present photometric and spectroscopic observations of the Type IIn supernova SN 2019zrk (also known as ZTF 20aacbyec). The SN shows a ≳ \gtrsim 100 day precursor, with a slow rise, followed by a rapid rise to M ≈ − 19.2 M\approx-19.2 in the r r and g g bands.

title: Multi-Hop Quantum Key Distribution with Passive Relays over Underwater Turbulence Channels
creator: Amir Hossein Fahim Raouf 1 , Majid Safari 2 and Murat Uysal 1
description: Abstract Absorption, scattering, and turbulence experienced in underwater channels severely limit the range of quantum communications. In this paper, to overcome range limitations, we investigate a multi-hop underwater quantum key distribution (QKD) where intermediate nodes help the key distribution between the source and destination nodes.

title: Optimal Clipping and Magnitude-aware Differentiation for Improved Quantization-aware Training
creator: Charbel Sakr, Steve Dai, Rangharajan Venkatesan, Brian Zimmer, William J. Dally, Brucek Khailany
description: Abstract Data clipping is crucial in reducing noise in quantization operations and improving the achievable accuracy of quantization-aware training (QAT). Current practices rely on heuristics to set clipping threshold scalars and cannot be shown to be optimal. We propose Optimally Clipped Tensors And Vectors (OCTAV), a recursive algorithm to determine MSE-optimal clipping scalars.

title: Estimating Pose from Pressure Data for Smart Beds with Deep Image-based Pose Estimators
creator: Vandad Davoodnia, Saeed Ghorbani, Ali Etemad
description: Abstract In-bed pose estimation has shown value in fields such as hospital patient monitoring, sleep studies, and smart homes. In this paper, we explore different strategies for detecting body pose from highly ambiguous pressure data, with the aid of pre-existing pose estimators.

title: Robust space-time finite element error estimates for parabolic distributed optimal control problems with energy regularization
creator: Ulrich Langer, Olaf Steinbach, Huidong Yang
description: Abstract We consider space-time tracking optimal control problems for linear parabolic initial boundary value problems that are given in the space-time cylinder Q = Ω × ( 0 , T ) Q=\Omega\times(0,T) , and that are controlled by the right-hand side z ϱ z_{\varrho} from the Bochner space L 2 ​ ( 0 , T , H − 1 ​

title: Fast Computation of Highly G G -Optimal Exact Designs via Particle Swarm Optimization
creator: Stephen J. Walsh, John J. Borkowski
description: Abstract Computing proposed exact G G -optimal designs for response surface models is a difficult computation that has received incremental improvements via algorithm development in the last two-decades. These optimal designs have not been considered widely in applications in part due to the difficulty and cost involved with computing them.

title: When quantum corrections alter the predictions of classical field theory for scalar field dark matter
creator: Andrew Eberhardt, Michael Kopp, Tom Abel
description: Abstract We investigate the timescale on which quantum corrections alter the predictions of classical field theory for scalar field dark matter. This is accomplished by including second order terms in the evolution proportional to the covariance of the field operators.

title: GLOBAL UNIFORM IN N ESTIMATES FOR SOLUTIONS OF A SYSTEM OF HARTREE–FOCK–BOGOLIUBOV TYPE IN THE GROSS–PITAVESKII REGIME.
creator: Xiaoqi Huang
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xiaoqi Huang. We extend the recent work of Chong et al., 2022 [ 7 ] to the critical case. More precisely, we prove global in time, uniform in N N estimates for the solutions ϕ \phi , Λ \Lambda and Γ \Gamma of a coupled system of Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov type with interaction potential 1 N ​ V N ​ ( x − y ) = N 2 ​ v ​ ( N ⁡ ( x − y ) ) \frac{1}{N}V_{N}(x-y)=N^{2}v(N(x-y)) .

title: An Abstract View on Optimizations in Propositional Frameworks
creator: YULIYA LIERLER
description: Abstract Search-optimization problems are plentiful in scientific and engineering domains. Artificial intelligence has long contributed to the development of search algorithms and declarative programming languages geared toward solving and modeling search-optimization problems. Automated reasoning and knowledge representation are the subfields of AI that are particularly vested in these developments.

title: A software toolkit and hardware platform for investigating and comparing robot autonomy algorithms in simulation and reality
creator: Asher Elmquist, Aaron Young, Ishaan Mahajan, Kyle Fahey, Abhiraj Dashora, Sriram Ashokkumar, Stefan Caldararu, Victor Freire, Xiangru Xu, Radu Serban, Dan Negrut
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Asher Elmquist, Aaron Young, Ishaan Mahajan, Kyle Fahey, Abhiraj Dashora, Sriram Ashokkumar, Stefan Caldararu, Victor Freire, Xiangru Xu, Radu Serban, Dan Negrut. We describe a software framework and a hardware platform used in tandem for the design and analysis of robot autonomy algorithms in simulation and reality.

title: Memory-Based Model Editing at Scale
creator: Eric Mitchell, Charles Lin, Antoine Bosselut, Christopher D Manning, Chelsea Finn
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Eric Mitchell, Charles Lin, Antoine Bosselut, Christopher D Manning, Chelsea Finn. Even the largest neural networks make errors, and once-correct predictions can become invalid as the world changes. Model editors make local updates to the behavior of base (pre-trained) models to inject updated knowledge or correct undesirable behaviors.

title: Implications of parity-violating electron scattering experiments on 48 Ca (CREX) and 208 Pb (PREX-II) for nuclear energy density functionals
creator: Esra Yüksel, Nils Paar
description: Abstract Recent precise parity-violating electron scattering experiments on 48 Ca (CREX) and 208 Pb (PREX-II) provide a new insight on the formation of neutron skin in nuclei. Within the energy density functional (EDF) framework, we investigate the implications of CREX and PREX-II data on nuclear matter symmetry energy and isovector properties of finite nuclei: neutron skin thickness and dipole polarizability.

title: Reconstruction of smooth shape defects in waveguides using locally resonant frequencies
creator: Angèle Niclas, Laurent Seppecher
description: Abstract This article aims to present a new method to reconstruct slowly varying width defects in 2D waveguides using locally resonant frequencies. At these frequencies, locally resonant modes propagate in the waveguide under the form of Airy functions depending on a parameter called the locally resonant point.

title: Sphere Packing Densities of Certain Families of Elliptic Curves
creator: Arjun Nigam
description: Abstract . In this paper, we examine the Mordell-Weil lattices of two families of elliptic curves over fields of characteristic p > 0 p>0 . We compute explicit lower bounds on the densest sphere packings of Mordell-Weil lattices using geometric information about the curve such as its Néron–Tate height and rational points on the curve.

title: Ultra-High-Precision Detection of Single Microwave Photons based on a Hybrid System between Majorana Zero Mode and a Quantum Dot
creator: Eric Chatterjee, Wei Pan, Daniel Soh
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Eric Chatterjee, Wei Pan, Daniel Soh. The ability to detect single photons has become increasingly essential due to the rise of photon-based quantum computing. In this theoretical work, we propose a system consisting of a quantum dot (QD) side-coupled to a superconducting nanowire. The coupling opens a gap in both the QD mode and the Majorana zero mode (MZM) at the nanowire edge, enabling photon absorption in the system.

title: Composite Quantum Simulations
creator: Matthew Hagan, Nathan Wiebe
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Matthew Hagan, Nathan Wiebe. In this paper we provide a framework for combining multiple quantum simulation methods, such as Trotter-Suzuki formulas and QDrift into a single Composite channel that builds upon older coalescing ideas for reducing gate counts. The central idea behind our approach is to use a partitioning scheme that allocates a Hamiltonian term to the Trotter or QDrift part of a channel within the simulation.

title: Impact of fragment formation on shear viscosity in the nuclear liquid-gas phase transition region
creator: X. G. Deng (邓先概) ID, P. Danielewicz ID, Y. G. Ma (马余刚) ID, H. Lin (林豪), Y. X. Zhang (张英逊) ID
description: Abstract Within the improved quantum molecular dynamic (ImQMD) model we follow the evolution of nuclear matter for planar Couette flow in a periodic box. We focus on the region of liquid-gas phase transition and extract the shear viscosity coefficient from the local stress tensor, directly following viscosity definition.

title: A Survey of Automated Data Augmentation Algorithms for Deep Learning-based Image Classification Tasks
creator: Zihan Yang, Richard O. Sinnott, James Bailey, Qiuhong Ke
description: Abstract In recent years, one of the most popular techniques in the computer vision community has been the deep learning technique. As a data-driven technique, deep model requires enormous amounts of accurately labelled training data, which is often inaccessible in many real-world applications. A data-space solution is Data Augmentation (DA), that can artificially generate new images out of original samples.

title: Zircons and smooth Bruhat intervals in symmetric groups
creator: Vincent Umutabazi
description: Abstract . In this paper, we prove that if the dual of a Bruhat interval in a Weyl group is a zircon, then that interval is rationally smooth. Investigating when the converse holds, and drawing inspiration from conjectures by Delanoy, leads us to pose two conjectures.

title: Sign-reversed anomalous Nernst effect in the ferromagnetic Weyl-semimetal Fe 3-δ GeTe 2 : the role of Fe vacancies
creator: Haiyang Yang, Qi Wang, Junwu Huang, Zhouliang Wang, Keqi Xia, Chao Cao, Mingliang Tian, Zhuan Xu, Jianhui Dai, Yuke Li
description: Abstract Anomalous Nernst effect, as a thermal partner of anomalous Hall effect, is particularly sensitive to the Berry curvature anomaly near the Fermi level, and has been used to probe the topological nature of quantum materials. In this work, we report the observation of both effects in the ferromagnetic Weyl-semimetal Fe 3-δ GeTe 2 with tunable Fe vacancies.

title: A Stochastic Proximal Method for Nonsmooth Regularized Finite Sum Optimization
creator: Dounia Lakhmiri dounia.lakhmiri@polymtl.ca, Dominique Orban dominique.orban@polymtl.ca, Andrea Lodi andra.lodi@cornell.edu
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Dounia Lakhmiri dounia.lakhmiri@polymtl.ca, Dominique Orban dominique.orban@polymtl.ca, Andrea Lodi andra.lodi@cornell.edu. We consider the problem of training a deep neural network with nonsmooth regularization to retrieve a sparse and efficient sub-structure. Our regularizer is only assumed to be lower semi-continuous and prox-bounded. We combine an adaptive quadratic regularization approach with proximal stochastic gradient principles to derive a new solver, called SR2, whose convergence and worst-case complexity are established without knowledge or approximation of the gradient’s Lipschitz constant.

title: F3 Hand: A Versatile Robot Hand Inspired by Human Thumb and Index Fingers
creator: Naoki Fukaya, Avinash Ummadisingu, Guilherme Maeda, Shin-ichi Maeda
description: Abstract It is challenging to grasp numerous objects with varying sizes and shapes with a single robot hand. To address this, we propose a new robot hand called the “F3 hand” inspired by the complex movements of human index finger and thumb.

title: Capillarity-driven thinning dynamics of entangled polymer solutions
creator: Jianyi Du, Hiroko Ohtani, Alper Kiziltas, Kevin Ellwood, Gareth H. McKinley
description: Abstract We analyze the capillarity-driven thinning dynamics of entangled polymer solutions described by the Doi-Edwards-Marrucci-Grizzuti (DEMG) model and the Rolie-Poly (RP) model. Both models capture polymer reptation, finite rates of chain retraction and finite extensibility of single polymer molecules, while differing slightly in their final form regarding to the convective constraint release.

title: Dynamics of temporal Kerr cavity solitons in the presence of rapid parameter inhomogeneities: from bichromatic driving to third-order dispersion
creator: Caleb Todd, Zongda Li, Stéphane Coen, Stuart G. Murdoch, Gian-Luca Oppo, Miro Erkintalo
description: Abstract Temporal Kerr cavity solitons are pulses of light that can persist in coherently-driven, dispersive resonators with Kerr-type nonlinearity. It is widely accepted that such solitons react to parameter inhomogeneities by experiencing a temporal drift whose rate is governed by the gradient of the parameter at the soliton’s position.

title: Learning the Dynamical Response of Nonlinear Non-Autonomous Dynamical Systems with Deep Operator Learning Neural Networks Journal: Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence
creator: Guang Lin, Christian Moya, Zecheng Zhang
description: Abstract We propose using operator learning to approximate the dynamical system response with control, such as nonlinear control systems. Unlike classical function learning, operator learning maps between two function spaces, does not require discretization of the output function, and provides flexibility in data preparation and solution prediction.

title: Monitoring Observations of SMC X-1’s Excursions (MOOSE) I: Program Description and Initial High-State Spectral Results 2022 Monitoring Observations of SMC X-1’s Excursions (MOOSE) I: Program Description and Initial High-State Spectral Results – References
creator: Kristen C. Dage McKinley Brumback, Joey Neilsen, Chin-Ping Hu, Diego Altamirano, Arash Bahramian, Philip A. Charles William I. Clarkson, Daryl Haggard, Ryan C. Hickox, Jamie Kennea
description: Abstract SMC X-1 has exhibited three super-orbital period excursions since the onset of X-ray monitoring beginning with RXTE’s launch in 1995. NICER has recently probed a fourth observed excursion beginning in 2021 with our program Monitoring Observations of SMC X-1’s Excursions (MOOSE). These sensitive new MOOSE data probe different super-orbital periods and phases within them.

title: Robust Distillation for Worst-class Performance
creator: Serena Wang, Harikrishna Narasimhan, Yichen Zhou, Sara Hooker, Michal Lukasik, Aditya Krishna Menon
description: Abstract Knowledge distillation has proven to be an effective technique in improving the performance a student model using predictions from a teacher model. However, recent work has shown that gains in average efficiency are not uniform across subgroups in the data, and in particular can often come at the cost of accuracy on rare subgroups and classes.

title: Determining g A / g V g_{A}/g_{V} with High Resolution Spectral Measurements Using an LiInSe 2 Bolometer
creator: A.F. Leder, D. Mayer, J. L. Ouellet, F. A. Danevich, L. Dumoulin, A. Giuliani, J. Kostensalo, J. Kotila, P. de Marcillac, C. Nones, V. Novati, E. Olivieri, D. Poda, J. Suhonen, V.I. Tretyak, L. Winslow, A. Zolotarova
description: Abstract Neutrinoless Double-Beta decay (0 ν ​ β ​ β \nu\beta\beta ) processes sample a wide range of intermediate forbidden nuclear transitions, which may be impacted by quenching of the axial vector coupling constant ( g A / g V g_{A}/g_{V} ), the uncertainty of which plays a pivotal role in determining the sensitivity reach of 0 ν ​ β

title: Repro Samples Method for Finite- and Large-Sample Inferences
creator: Min-ge Xie, Peng Wang
description: Abstract This article presents a novel, general, and effective simulation-inspired approach, called repro samples method , to conduct statistical inference. The approach studies the performance of artificial samples, referred to as repro samples , obtained by mimicking the true observed sample to achieve uncertainty quantification and construct confidence sets for parameters of interest with guaranteed coverage rates.

title: Individual addressing of trapped ion qubits with geometric phase gates
creator: R. T. Sutherland, R. Srinivas, D. T. C. Allcock
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by R. T. Sutherland, R. Srinivas, D. T. C. Allcock. We propose a new scheme for individual addressing of trapped ion qubits, selecting them via their motional frequency. We show that geometric phase gates can perform single-qubit rotations using the coherent interference of spin-independent and (global) spin-dependent forces. The spin-independent forces, which can be generated via localised electric fields, increase the gate speed while reducing its sensitivity to motional decoherence, which we show analytically and numerically.

title: Single production of vectorlike T T quark at future high-energy linear e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} collider
creator: Lin Han 1 , Liu-Feng Du 2 , Yao-Bei Liu 2
description: Abstract Based on a model-independent framework including the vectorlike top partner (VLQ- T T ), we investigate the prospect of discovering the singlet or doublet VLQ- T T via the single production process e − ​ e + → T ​ t ¯ + t ​ T ¯ e^{-}e^{+}\to T\bar{t}+t\bar{T} with the T → Z ​ t T\to Zt decay

title: Dynamics and steady state of squirmer motion in liquid crystal
creator: Leonid Berlyand, Hai Chi, Mykhailo Potomkin, Nung Kwan Yip
description: Abstract We analyze a nonlinear PDE system describing the motion of a microswimmer in a nematic liquid crystal environment. For the microswimmer’s motility, the squirmer model is used in which self-propulsion enters the model through the slip velocity on the microswimmer’s surface. The liquid crystal is described using the well-established Beris-Edwards formulation.

title: ℛ ⁡ ( p , q ) − \mathcal{R}(p,q)- deformed super Virasoro n − n- algebra
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by . In this paper, we construct the super Witt algebra and super Virasoro algebra in the framework of the ℛ ⁡ ( p , q ) − \mathcal{R}(p,q)- deformed quantum algebras. Moreover, we perform the super ℛ ⁡ ( p , q ) − \mathcal{R}(p,q)- deformed Witt n − n- algebra, the ℛ ⁡ ( p , q ) − \mathcal{R}(p,q)- deformed Virasoro n − n- algebra and discuss the super ℛ ⁡ ( p , q ) − \mathcal{R}(p,q)- Virasoro n − n-

title: Physics Informed Neural Fields for Smoke Reconstruction with Sparse Data Journal: TOG Journal: TOG Volume: 41 4 119 7 DOI: 10.1145/3528223.3530169 CCS: Computing methodologies Neural networks CCS: Computing methodologies Physical simulation
creator: Mengyu Chu, Lingjie Liu, Quan Zheng, Erik Franz, Hans-Peter Seidel, Christian Theobalt, Rhaleb Zayer
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Mengyu Chu, Lingjie Liu, Quan Zheng, Erik Franz, Hans-Peter Seidel, Christian Theobalt, Rhaleb Zayer. High-fidelity reconstruction of dynamic fluids from sparse multiview RGB videos remains a formidable challenge, due to the complexity of the underlying physics as well as the severe occlusion and complex lighting in the captured data. Existing solutions either assume knowledge of obstacles and lighting, or only focus on simple fluid scenes without obstacles or complex lighting, and thus are unsuitable for real-world scenes with unknown lighting conditions or arbitrary obstacles.

title: Existence and uniqueness of the globally conservative solutions for a weakly dissipative Camassa-Holm equation in time weighted H 1 ​ ( ℝ ) H^{1}(\mathbb{R}) space
creator: Zhiying Meng and, Zhaoyang Yin
description: Abstract In this paper, we prove that the existence and uniqueness of globally weak solutions to the Cauchy problem for the weakly dissipative Camassa-Holm equation in time weighted H 1 H^{1} space. First, we derive an equivalent semi-linear system by introducing some new variables, and present the globally conservative solutions of this equation in time weighted H 1 H^{1} space.

title: Mass and Expansion of Asymptotically Conical Kähler Metrics
creator: Qi Yao
description: Abstract . We prove an expansion theorem on scalar-flat asymptotically conical (AC) Kähler metrics. The ADM mass is known to be defined in ALE Riemannian manifolds. The concept of ADM mass can be generalized to AC cases. Consider an AC Kähler manifold with asymptotic to a Ricci-flat Kähler metric cone with complex dimension n n .

title: Chiral SQUID-metamaterial waveguide for circuit-QED
creator: Xin Wang, Ya-Fen Lin, Jia-Qi Li, Wen-Xiao Liu, Hong-Rong Li
description: Abstract Superconducting metamaterials, which are designed and fabricated with structured fundamental circuit elements, have motivated recent developments of exploring unconventional quantum phenomena in circuit quantum electrodynamics (circuit-QED). We propose a method to engineer 1D Josephson metamaterial as a chiral waveguide by considering a programmed spatiotemporal modulation on its effective impedance.

title: Towards Analytic Structure of Feynman Parameter Integrals with Rational Curves
creator: Jianyu Gong, and Ellis Ye Yuan
description: Abstract We propose a strategy to study the analytic structure of Feynman parameter integrals where singularities of the integrand consist of rational irreducible components. At the core of this strategy is the identification of a selected stratum of discontinuities induced from the integral, together with a geometric method for computing their singularities on the principle sheet.

title: Distributed and Distribution-Robust Meta Reinforcement Learning (D 2 -RMRL) for Data Pre-storing and Routing in Cube Satellite Networks Y. Hu is with the Department of Electrical Engineering, Columbia University, New York, NY, USA, 24061, and the Wireless@VT, Bradley Department of Electrical and Com
creator: Ye Hu, Xiaodong Wang, Fellow, IEEE , Walid Saad, Fellow, IEEE
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ye Hu, Xiaodong Wang, Fellow, IEEE , Walid Saad, Fellow, IEEE. In this paper, the problem of data pre-storing and routing in dynamic, resource-constrained cube satellite networks is studied. In such a network, each cube satellite delivers requested data to user clusters under its coverage. A group of ground gateways will route and pre-store certain data to the satellites, such that the ground users can be directly served with the pre-stored data.

title: Transformers are Meta-Reinforcement Learners
creator: Luckeciano C. Melo
description: Abstract The transformer architecture and variants presented a remarkable success across many machine learning tasks in recent years. This success is intrinsically related to the capability of handling long sequences and the presence of context-dependent weights from the attention mechanism. We argue that these capabilities suit the central role of a Meta-Reinforcement Learning algorithm.

title: Deep Isolation Forest for Anomaly Detection
creator: Hongzuo Xu, Guansong Pang, Yijie Wang and Yongjun Wang
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Hongzuo Xu, Guansong Pang, Yijie Wang and Yongjun Wang. Isolation forest (iForest) has been emerging as arguably the most popular anomaly detector in recent years due to its general effectiveness across different benchmarks and strong scalability. Nevertheless, its linear axis-parallel isolation method often leads to (i) failure in detecting hard anomalies that are difficult to isolate in high-dimensional/non-linear-separable data space, and (ii) notorious algorithmic bias that assigns unexpectedly lower anomaly scores to artefact regions. These issues contribute to high false negative errors.

title: A detailed temperature map of the archetypal protostellar shocks in L1157 Journal: ApJL astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ) , Numpy ( van der Walt et al. 2011 ) , CASA ( McMullin et al. 2007 , v5.4.0; v5.6.1;) , bettermoments ( Teague & Foreman-Mackey 2018 , v1.0.0; ) , HfS ( Estalella 201
creator: S. Feng (Chinese Name), H. B. Liu, P. Caselli, A. Burkhardt, F. Du, R. Bachiller, C. Codella, C. Ceccarelli
description: Abstract We present sensitive NH 3 \rm NH_{3} (1,1)–(7,7) line images from the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array toward successive shocks, which are associated with the blueshifted outflow lobe driven by the compact protobinary system L1157. Within a projection distance of 0.

title: Fermionic DIS from a deformed string/gauge correspondence model
creator: Eduardo Folco Capossoli 1, Miguel Angel Martín Contreras 2, Danning Li 3, Alfredo Vega 2, Henrique Boschi-Filho 4
description: Abstract From a deformed AdS 5 space, we used the string/gauge duality to study the deep inelastic scattering for unpolarized fermions with spin 1/2, considering the large Bjorken x x parameter regime. Here, we also took into account an anomalous dimension of an operator which represents fermions at the boundary.

title: Permutation Search of Tensor Network Structures via Local Sampling
creator: Chao Li, Junhua Zeng, Zerui Tao, Qibin Zhao
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Chao Li, Junhua Zeng, Zerui Tao, Qibin Zhao. Recent works put much effort into tensor network structure search (TN-SS), aiming to select suitable tensor network (TN) structures, involving the TN-ranks, formats, and so on, for the decomposition or learning tasks. In this paper, we consider a practical variant of TN-SS, dubbed TN permutation search (TN-PS), in which we search for good mappings from tensor modes onto TN vertices (core tensors) for compact TN representations.

title: Chemical and Physical Characterization of the Isolated Protostellar Source CB68: FAUST. IV Journal: ApJ
creator: Muneaki Imai, Yoko Oya, Brian Svoboda, Hauyu Baobab Liu, Bertrand Lefloch, Serena Viti, Yichen Zhang, Cecilia Ceccarelli, Claudio Codella, Claire J. Chandler, Nami Sakai, Yuri Aikawa, Felipe O. Alves, Nadia Balucani, Eleonora Bianchi, Mathilde Bouvier, Gemma Busquet, Paola Caselli, Emmanuel Caux, St
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Muneaki Imai, Yoko Oya, Brian Svoboda, Hauyu Baobab Liu, Bertrand Lefloch, Serena Viti, Yichen Zhang, Cecilia Ceccarelli, Claudio Codella, Claire J. Chandler, Nami Sakai, Yuri Aikawa, Felipe O. Alves, Nadia Balucani, Eleonora Bianchi, Mathilde Bouvier, Gemma Busquet, Paola Caselli, Emmanuel Caux, St. Chemical diversity of low-mass protostellar sources has so far been recognized, and environmental effects are invoked as its origin. In this context, observations of isolated protostellar sources without influences of nearby objects are of particular importance.

title: Safe Output Feedback Motion Planning from Images via Learned Perception Modules and Contraction Theory
creator: Glen Chou, Necmiye Ozay, Dmitry Berenson
description: Abstract We present a motion planning algorithm for a class of uncertain control-affine nonlinear systems which guarantees runtime safety and goal reachability when using high-dimensional sensor measurements (e.g., RGB-D images) and a learned perception module in the feedback control loop.

title: On a Mathematical Model of the Rotating Atmosphere of the Earth
creator: Tetu Makino
description: Abstract In meteorology the analysis of motions of the atmosphere on the Earth has been done using various mathematical models and using various approximations. In this article as the simplest model the compressible Euler equations with barotropic equation of state of the ideal gas is analyzed under the co-ordinate system which rotates with constant angular velocity.
