But this reliance can be abused—strategic machines might craft representations that manipulate their users. How can a user make good choices based on strategic representations? We formalize this as a learning problem, and pursue algorithms for decision-making that are robust to manipulation.

title: Rarity Score : A New Metric to Evaluate the Uncommonness of Synthesized Images
creator: Jiyeon Han, Hwanil Choi, Yunjey Choi, Junho Kim, Jung-Woo Ha, Jaesik Choi
description: Abstract Evaluation metrics in image synthesis play a key role to measure performances of generative models. However, most metrics mainly focus on image fidelity. Existing diversity metrics are derived by comparing distributions, and thus they cannot quantify the diversity or rarity degree of each generated image.

title: A halo of trapped interstellar matter surrounding the solar system
creator: Jorge Peñarrubia
description: Abstract This paper shows that gravitating bodies travelling through the Galaxy can trap lighter interstellar particles that pass nearby with small relative velocities onto temporarily-bound orbits. The capture mechanism is driven by the Galactic tidal field, which can decelerate infalling objects to a degree where their binding energy becomes negative.

title: Bio-inspired Intelligence with Applications to Robotics: A Survey
creator: Junfei Li, Zhe Xu, Danjie Zhu, Kevin Dong, Tao Yan, Zhu Zeng, Simon X. Yang
description: Abstract In the past decades, considerable attention has been paid to bio-inspired intelligence and its applications to robotics. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of bio-inspired intelligence, with a focus on neurodynamics approaches, to various robotic applications, particularly to path planning and control of autonomous robotic systems.

title: COVID-19 Detection using Transfer Learning with Convolutional Neural Network
creator: Pramit Dutta 1 , Tanny Roy 2 and Nafisa Anjum 3
description: Abstract The Novel Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is a fatal infectious disease, first recognized in December 2019 in Wuhan, Hubei, China, and has gone on an epidemic situation. Under these circumstances, it became more important to detect COVID-19 in infected people. Nowadays, the testing kits are gradually lessening in number compared to the number of infected population.

title: SOS: Score-based Oversampling for Tabular Data Conference: Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 14–18, 2022; Washington, DC, USA Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD ’22), August 14–18, 2022,
creator: Jayoung Kim, Chaejeong Lee, Yehjin Shin, Sewon Park, Minjung Kim, Noseong Park, Jihoon Cho
description: Abstract . Score-based generative models (SGMs) are a recent breakthrough in generating fake images. SGMs are known to surpass other generative models, e.g., generative adversarial networks (GANs) and variational autoencoders (VAEs). Being inspired by their big success, in this work, we fully customize them for generating fake tabular data.

title: Study of the resonance structures in 𝒆 + ​ 𝒆 − → 𝝅 + ​ 𝝅 − ​ 𝑱 / 𝝍 e^{+}e^{-}\rightarrow\pi^{+}\pi^{-}J/\psi process
creator: M. Ablikim 1 , M. N. Achasov 10,b , P. Adlarson 68 , M. Albrecht 4 , R. Aliberti 28 , A. Amoroso 67A,67C , M. R. An 32 , Q. An 64,50 , X. H. Bai 58 , Y. Bai 49 , O. Bakina 29 , R. Baldini Ferroli 23A , I. Balossino 24A , Y. Ban 39,h , V. Batozskaya 1,37 , D. Becker 28 , K. Begzsuren 26 , N. Berger 2
description: Abstract Using about 23 fb − 1 \mathrm{fb^{-1}} of data collected with the BESIII detector operating at the BEPCII storage ring, a precise measurement of the e + ​ e − → π + ​ π − ​ J / ψ e^{+}e^{-}\rightarrow\pi^{+}\pi^{-}J/\psi Born cross section is performed at center-of-mass energies from 3.7730 to 4.7008 GeV.

title: Axial vectors in DarkCast
creator: Chaja Baruch, Philip Ilten, Yotam Soreq, Mike Williams
description: Abstract In this work, we explore new spin-1 states with axial couplings to the standard model fermions. We develop a data-driven method to estimate their hadronic decay rates based on data from τ \tau decays and using SU(3) flavor symmetry. We derive the current and future experimental constraints for several benchmark models.

title: Identifying Counterfeit Products using Blockchain Technology in Supply Chain System PubID: pubid: 978-1-6654-2678-7/22/$31.00 ©2022 IEEE
creator: Nafisa Anjum, Pramit Dutta
description: Abstract With the advent of globalization and the ever-growing rate of technology, the volume of production as well as ease of procuring counterfeit goods has become unprecedented. Be it food, drug or luxury items, all kinds of industrial manufacturers and distributors are now seeking greater transparency in supply chain operations with a view to deter counterfeiting.

title: A matter wave Rarity-Tapster interferometer to demonstrate non-locality
creator: Kieran F. Thomas, Bryce M. Henson, Yu Wang, Robert J. Lewis-Swan, Karen V. Kheruntsyan, Sean S. Hodgman, Andrew G. Truscott
description: Abstract We present an experimentally viable approach to demonstrating quantum non-locality in a matter wave system via a Rarity-Tapster interferometer using two s s -wave scattering halos generated by colliding helium Bose-Einstein condensates. The theoretical basis for this method is discussed, and its suitability is experimentally quantified.

title: Rules Ensemble Method with Group Lasso for Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Estimation
creator: Ke Wan, Kensuke Tanioka, Toshio Shimokawa
description: Abstract The increasing scientific attention given to precision medicine based on real-world data has led many recent studies to clarify the relationships between treatment effects and patient characteristics. However, this is challenging because of ubiquitous heterogeneity in the treatment effect for individuals and the real-world data on their backgrounds being complex and noisy.

title: Exploring universal characteristics of neutron star matter with relativistic ab initio equations of state
creator: Sibo Wang, Chencan Wang, Hui Tong
description: Abstract Starting from the relativistic realistic nucleon-nucleon ( N ​ N NN ) interactions, the relativistic Brueckner-Hartree-Fock (RBHF) theory in the full Dirac space is employed to study neutron star properties. First, the one-to-one correspondence relation for gravitational redshift and mass is established and used to infer the masses of isolated neutron stars by combining gravitational redshift measurements.

title: Chromatic polynomials of signed book graphs
creator: Deepak Sehrawat, Bikash Bhattacharjya
description: Abstract Abstract For m\geq 3 and n\geq 1 , the m -cycle book graph B(m,n) consists of n copies of the cycle C_{m} with one common edge. In this paper, we prove that (a) the number of switching non-isomorphic signed B(m,n) is n+1 , and (b) the chromatic number of a signed B(m,n) is either 2 or 3.

title: HairFIT: Pose-Invariant Hairstyle Transfer via Flow-based Hair Alignment and Semantic-Region-Aware Inpainting
creator: Chaeyeon Chung, Taewoo Kim, Hyelin Nam, Seunghwan Choi, Gyojung Gu, Sunghyun Park, Jaegul Choo
description: Abstract Hairstyle transfer is the task of modifying a source hairstyle to a target one. Although recent hairstyle transfer models can reflect the delicate features of hairstyles, they still have two major limitations. First, the existing methods fail to transfer hairstyles when a source and a target image have different poses ( e.

title: Prototyping fast and agile motions for legged robots with Horizon
creator: Francesco Ruscelli, Arturo Laurenzi, Nikos G. Tsagarakis, Enrico Mingo Hoffman
description: Abstract For legged robots to perform agile, highly dynamic and contact-rich motions, whole-body trajectories computation of under-actuated complex systems subject to non-linear dynamics is required. In this work, we present hands-on applications of Horizon , a novel open-source framework for trajectory optimization tailored to robotic systems, that provides a collection of tools to simplify dynamic motion generation.

title: Automatic Correction of Human Translations
creator: Jessy Lin Geza Kovacs Aditya Shastry, Joern Wuebker John DeNero
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jessy Lin Geza Kovacs Aditya Shastry, Joern Wuebker John DeNero. We introduce translation error correction (TEC), the task of automatically correcting human-generated translations. Imperfections in machine translations (MT) have long motivated systems for improving translations post-hoc with automatic post-editing. In contrast, little attention has been devoted to the problem of automatically correcting human translations, despite the intuition that humans make distinct errors that machines would be well-suited to assist with, from typos to inconsistencies in translation conventions.

title: Search for 𝑿 ⁡ ( 𝟑𝟖𝟕𝟐 ) → 𝝅 + ​ 𝝅 − ​ 𝝅 𝟎 X(3872)\to\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0} at Belle
creator: J. H. Yin, E. Won, I. Adachi, H. Aihara, S. Al Said, D. M. Asner, H. Atmacan, V. Aulchenko, T. Aushev, R. Ayad, V. Babu, S. Bahinipati, P. Behera, K. Belous, J. Bennett, M. Bessner, V. Bhardwaj, B. Bhuyan, T. Bilka, D. Bodrov, G. Bonvicini, J. Borah, A. Bozek, M. Bračko, P. Branchini, T. E. Browder,
description: Abstract We present a search for the decay X ⁡ ( 3872 ) → π + ​ π − ​ π 0 X(3872)\to\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0} in the ( 772 ± 11 ) × 10 6 (772\pm 11)\times 10^{6} Υ ⁡ ( 4 ​ S ) → B ​ B ¯ \Upsilon(4S)\to B\bar{B} data sample collected at the Belle detector, where the X

title: Beating Poisson stochastic particle encapsulation in flow-focusing microfluidic devices using viscoelastic liquids
creator: Keshvad Shahrivar, Francesco Del Giudice
description: Abstract The encapsulation and co-encapsulation of particles in microfluidic flows is essential in applications related to single-cell analysis and material synthesis. However, the whole encapsulation process is stochastic in nature, and its efficiency is limited by the so-called Poisson limit.

title: The Longest Delay: a 14.5 Yr Campaign to Determine the Third Time Delay in the Lensing Cluster SDSS J1004+4112
creator: J.A. Muñoz, C.S. Kochanek, J. Fohlmeister, J. Wambsganss, E. Falco, R. Forés-Toribio
description: Abstract We present new light curves for the four bright images of the five image cluster-lensed quasar gravitational lens system SDSS J1004+4112. The light curves span 14.5 yr and allow measurement of the time delay between the trailing bright quasar image D and the leading image C.

title: Medical Dialogue Response Generation with Pivotal Information Recalling Conference: Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 14–18, 2022; Washington, DC, USA Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD
creator: Yu Zhao, Yunxin Li, Yuxiang Wu, Baotian Hu, Qingcai Chen, Xiaolong Wang, Yuxin Ding, Min Zhang
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yu Zhao, Yunxin Li, Yuxiang Wu, Baotian Hu, Qingcai Chen, Xiaolong Wang, Yuxin Ding, Min Zhang. Medical dialogue generation is an important yet challenging task. Most previous works rely on the attention mechanism and large-scale pretrained language models. However, these methods often fail to acquire pivotal information from the long dialogue history to yield an accurate and informative response, due to the fact that the medical entities usually scatters throughout multiple utterances along with the complex relationships between them.

title: Nucleosynthesis Contribution of Neutrino-dominated Accretion Flows to the Chemical Evolution of Active Galactic Nuclei
creator: Yan-Qing Qi, Tong Liu, Zhen-Yi Cai, Mouyuan Sun
description: Abstract Recent observations of quasars show high line-flux ratios in their broad emission lines and the ratios appear to be independent of redshift up to z ≳ 6 z\gtrsim 6 , which indicate that the broad-line regions of these early quasars are surprisingly metal-rich. Here, we revisit the chemical evolution of high-redshift quasars by adding a new ingredient, i.e.

title: Understanding Aesthetics with Language: A Photo Critique Dataset for Aesthetic Assessment
creator: Daniel Vera Nieto, Luigi Celona, Clara Fernandez-Labrador
description: Abstract Computational inference of aesthetics is an ill-defined task due to its subjective nature. Many datasets have been proposed to tackle the problem by providing pairs of images and aesthetic scores based on human ratings. However, humans are better at expressing their opinion, taste, and emotions by means of language rather than summarizing them in a single number.

title: Gauge invariance of the local phase in the Aharonov-Bohm interference: quantum electrodynamic approach
creator: Kicheon Kang
description: Abstract In the Aharonov-Bohm (AB) effect, interference fringes are observed for a charged particle in the absence of the local overlap with the external electromagnetic field. This notion of the apparent “nonlocality” of the interaction or the significant role of the potential has recently been challenged and are under debate.

title: Theory of ultrafast magnetization of non-magnetic semiconductors with localized conduction bands
creator: Giovanni Marini, Matteo Calandra
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Giovanni Marini, Matteo Calandra. The magnetization of a non-magnetic semiconductor by femtosecond light pulses is crucial to achieve an all-optical control of the spin dynamics in materials and to develop faster memory devices. However, the conditions for its detection are largely unknown. In this work we identify the criteria for the observation of ultrafast magnetization and critically discuss the difficulties hindering its experimental detection.

title: Multiscale Modelling of the Antiferromagnet Mn 2 Au: From ab-initio to Micromagnetics
creator: Joel Hirst, Unai Atxitia, Sergiu Ruta, Jerome Jackson, Leon Petit, Thomas Ostler
description: Abstract Antiferromagnets (AFMs) are strong candidates for the future spintronic and memory applications largely because of their inherently fast dynamics and lack of stray fields, with Mn 2 Au being one of the most promising. For the numerical modelling of magnetic material properties, it is common to use ab-initio methods, atomistic models and micromagnetics.

title: MSDF: A General Open-Domain Multi-Skill Dialog Framework
creator: Yu Zhao, Xinshuo Hu, Yunxin Li, Baotian Hu✉, Dongfang Li, Sichao Chen, Xiaolong Wang
description: Abstract Dialog systems have achieved significant progress and have been widely used in various scenarios. The previous researches mainly focused on designing dialog generation models in a single scenario, while comprehensive abilities are required to handle tasks under various scenarios in the real world.

title: The Wavefront Sets of Unipotent Supercuspidal Representations
creator: Dan Ciubotaru, Lucas Mason-Brown, Emile Okada
description: Abstract Let 𝐆 ⁡ ( 𝗄 ) \mathbf{G}({\mathsf{k}}) be a semisimple p p -adic group, inner to split. In this article, we compute the algebraic and canonical unramified wavefront sets of the irreducible supercuspidal representations of 𝐆 ⁡ ( 𝗄 ) \mathbf{G}({\mathsf{k}}) in Lusztig’s category of unipotent representations.

title: On Computing Optimal Linear Diagrams
creator: Alexander Dobler, Martin Nöllenburg
description: Abstract Linear diagrams are an effective way to visualize set-based data by representing elements as columns and sets as rows with one or more horizontal line segments, whose vertical overlaps with other rows indicate set intersections and their contained elements. The efficacy of linear diagrams heavily depends on having few line segments.

title: Study of Complex Absorption and Reflection in a Unique Intermediate Polar Paloma Facilities: XMM-Newton, NuSTAR HEASoft ( Nasa High Energy Astrophysics Science Archive Research Center (2014) Heasarc , https://heasarc.gsfc.nasa.gov/docs/software/heasoft/ ), XMM-Newton SAS ( https://www.cosmos.esa.int
creator: Anirban Dutta, Vikram Rana
description: Abstract We present the broadband (0.3-40.0 keV) X-ray analysis of a unique intermediate polar Paloma using simultaneous data from XMM-Newton and NuSTAR observatories. The X-ray power spectra show strong modulations over orbital period compared to spin period. The orbit folded lightcurves show single broad hump like structure with strong dips for soft to medium X-rays (0.3-10.0 keV).

title: Discrete Orthogonal Ensemble on the Exponential Lattices
creator: Shi-Hao Li, Bo-Jian Shen, Guo-Fu Yu, Peter J. Forrester
description: Abstract . Inspired by Aomoto’s q q -Selberg integral, the orthogonal ensemble in the exponential lattice is considered in this paper. By introducing a skew symmetric kernel, the configuration space of this ensemble is constructed to be symmetric and thus, corresponding skew inner product, skew orthogonal polynomials as well as correlation functions are explicitly formulated.

title: Dynamics of a dispersively coupled transmon qubit in the presence of a noise source embedded in the control line
creator: Antti Vaaranta, Marco Cattaneo, Russell E. Lake
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Antti Vaaranta, Marco Cattaneo, Russell E. Lake. We describe transmon qubit dynamics in the presence of noise introduced by an impedance-matched resistor ( 50 ​ Ω 50\,\mathrm{\Omega} ) that is embedded in the qubit control line. To obtain the time evolution, we rigorously derive the circuit Hamiltonian of the qubit, readout resonator and resistor by describing the latter as an infinite collection of bosonic modes through the Caldeira-Leggett model.

title: A Hybrid Modelling Approach for Aerial Manipulators
creator: Paul Kremer ✉, Jose Luis Sanchez-Lopez, Holger Voos
description: Abstract Aerial manipulators (AM) exhibit particularly challenging, non-linear dynamics; the UAV and the manipulator it is carrying form a tightly coupled dynamic system, mutually impacting each other. The mathematical model describing these dynamics forms the core of many solutions in non-linear control and deep reinforcement learning.

title: Local Slot Attention for Vision-and-Language Navigation Conference: Proceedings of the 2022 International Conference on Multimedia Retrieval; June 27–30, 2022; Newark, NJ, USA. Proceedings of the 2022 Int’l Conference on Multimedia Retrieval (ICMR ’22), June 27–30, 2022, Newark, NJ, USA DOI: 10.1145
creator: Yifeng Zhuang, Qiang Sun, Yanwei Fu, Lifeng Chen, Xiangyang Xue
description: Abstract . Vision-and-language navigation (VLN), a frontier study aiming to pave the way for general-purpose robots, has been a hot topic in the computer vision and natural language processing community. The VLN task requires an agent to navigate to a goal location following natural language instructions in unfamiliar environments. Recently, transformer-based models have gained significant improvements on the VLN task.

title: Study of polarization for even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states in SU(4) Graphene
creator: Moumita Indra 1, Dwipesh Majumder 2
description: Abstract We have focussed to study the even-denominator fractional quantum Hall (EDFQH) states observed in monolayer graphene. In this letter, we have studied polarization mainly for the two EDFQH states at filling fractions ν = 1 / 2 , 1 / 4 \nu=1/2,1/4 , which are observed in an experimental study [ \color blue Nat. Phys.

title: An efficient spectral method for the fractional Schrödinger equation on the real line
creator: Mengxia Shen, Haiyong Wang
description: Abstract The fractional Schrödinger equation (FSE) on the real line arises in a broad range of physical settings and their numerical simulation is challenging due to the nonlocal nature and the power law decay of the solution at infinity. In this paper, we propose a new spectral discretization scheme for the FSE in space based upon Malmquist-Takenaka functions.

title: Physics Informed Neural Networks for Two Dimensional Incompressible Thermal Convection Problems
creator: Atakan Aygun, Ali Karakus
description: Abstract Abstract Physics informed neural networks (PINNs) have drawn attention in recent years in engineering problems due to their effectiveness and ability to tackle the problems without generating complex meshes. PINNs use automatic differentiation to evaluate differential operators in conservation laws and hence do not need to have a discretization scheme.

title: All mistakes are not equal: Comprehensive Hierarchy Aware Multi-label Predictions (CHAMP)
creator: Ashwin Vaswani, Gaurav Aggarwal, Praneeth Netrapalli, Narayan G Hegde
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ashwin Vaswani, Gaurav Aggarwal, Praneeth Netrapalli, Narayan G Hegde. This paper considers the problem of Hierarchical Multi-Label Classification (HMC), where (i) several labels can be present for each example, and (ii) labels are related via a domain-specific hierarchy tree. Guided by the intuition that all mistakes are not equal, we present Comprehensive Hierarchy Aware Multi-label Predictions (CHAMP), a framework that penalizes a misprediction depending on its severity as per the hierarchy tree.

title: PICO: Pipeline Inference Framework for Versatile CNNs on Diverse Mobile Devices
creator: Xiang Yang, Zikang Xu, Qi Qi, Jingyu Wang, Haifeng Sun, Jianxin Liao, and Song Guo
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xiang Yang, Zikang Xu, Qi Qi, Jingyu Wang, Haifeng Sun, Jianxin Liao, and Song Guo. Distributing the inference of convolutional neural network (CNN) to multiple mobile devices has been studied in recent years to achieve real-time inference without losing accuracy. However, how to map CNN to devices remains a challenge. On the one hand, scheduling the workload of state-of-the-art CNNs with multiple devices is NP-Hard because the structures of CNNs are directed acyclic graphs (DAG) rather than simple chains.

title: A Deep Learning Approach for the Segmentation of Electroencephalography Data in Eye Tracking Applications
creator: Lukas Wolf, Ard Kastrati, Martyna Beata Płomecka, Jie-Ming Li, Dustin Klebe, Alexander Veicht, Roger Wattenhofer, Nicolas Langer
description: Abstract The collection of eye gaze information provides a window into many critical aspects of human cognition, health and behaviour. Additionally, many neuroscientific studies complement the behavioural information gained from eye tracking with the high temporal resolution and neurophysiological markers provided by electroencephalography (EEG).

title: The infinite dihedral group
creator: Jānis Buls
description: Abstract We describe the infinite dihedral group as automaton group. We collect basic results and give full proofs in details for all statements. Keywords automata (machines) groups, the infinite dihedral group 1. Preliminaries We use standard conventions. Nethertheless we recall some notation. For more details see [1].

The third author has been also support

title: BITS Pilani at HinglishEval: Quality Evaluation for Code-Mixed Hinglish Text Using Transformers
creator: Shaz Furniturewala, Vijay Kumari, Amulya Ratna Dash, Hriday Kedia
description: Abstract Code-Mixed text data consists of sentences having words or phrases from more than one language. Most multi-lingual communities worldwide communicate using multiple languages, with English usually one of them. Hinglish is a Code-Mixed text composed of Hindi and English but written in Roman script.

title: Understanding Robust Overfitting of Adversarial Training and Beyond
creator: Chaojian Yu, Bo Han, Li Shen, Jun Yu, Chen Gong, Mingming Gong, Tongliang Liu
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Chaojian Yu, Bo Han, Li Shen, Jun Yu, Chen Gong, Mingming Gong, Tongliang Liu. Robust overfitting widely exists in adversarial training of deep networks. The exact underlying reasons for this are still not completely understood. Here, we explore the causes of robust overfitting by comparing the data distribution of non-overfit (weak adversary) and overfitted (strong adversary) adversarial training, and observe that the distribution of the adversarial data generated by weak adversary mainly contain small-loss data.

title: Influence of the surface states on the nonlinear Hall effect in Weyl semimetals
creator: Diego García Ovalle, Armando Pezo, Aurélien Manchon
description: Abstract We investigate the influence of surface states on the nonlinear Hall response of non-centrosymmetric time-reversal invariant Weyl semimetals. To do so, we perform a tomography of the Berry curvature dipole in a slab system using a minimal two-band model.

title: AggNet: Learning to Aggregate Faces for Group Membership Verification
creator: Marzieh Gheisari, Javad Amirian, Teddy Furon, Laurent Amsaleg
description: Abstract In some face recognition applications, we are interested to verify whether an individual is a member of a group, without revealing their identity. Some existing methods, propose a mechanism for quantizing precomputed face descriptors into discrete embeddings and aggregating them into one group representation.

title: Towards Human-Level Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation with Reinforcement Learning
description: Abstract Achieving human-level dexterity is an important open problem in robotics. However, tasks of dexterous hand manipulation, even at the baby level, are challenging to solve through reinforcement learning (RL). The difficulty lies in the high degrees of freedom and the required cooperation among heterogeneous agents (e.g., joints of fingers).

title: You Only Derive Once (YODO): Automatic Differentiation for Efficient Sensitivity Analysis in Bayesian Networks
creator: \Name Rafael Ballester-Ripoll \Email rafael.ballester@ie.edu, \Name Manuele Leonelli \Email manuele.leonelli@ie.edu
description: Abstract Sensitivity analysis measures the influence of a Bayesian network’s parameters on a quantity of interest defined by the network, such as the probability of a variable taking a specific value. In particular, the so-called sensitivity value measures the quantity of interest’s partial derivative with respect to the network’s conditional probabilities.

title: Hyperverse, 5-dimensional gravity and multiverses as nested Gogberashvili shells
creator: Igor Yu. Potemine
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Igor Yu. Potemine. We consider the Hyperverse as a collection of multiverses in 5-dimensional spacetime with gravitational constant G G . Each multiverse in our simplified model is a bouquet of nested spherical Gogberashvili shells. If g k g_{k} is the gravitational constant of a thin shell S k S_{k} and ε k \varepsilon_{k} its thickness then G ∼ ε k ​ g k G\sim\varepsilon_{k}g_{k} .

title: Bubble nucleation and quantum initial conditions in classical statistical simulations
creator: Anders Tranberg, Gerhard Ungersbäck
description: Abstract Classical-statistical lattice simulations provide a useful approximation to out-of-equilibrium quantum field theory, but only for systems exhibiting large occupation numbers, and only for phenomena that are not intrinsically quantum mechanical in nature. In certain special circumstances, it can be appropriate to initialize such real-time simulations with quantum-like zero-point fluctuations.

title: Time dynamics of multi-photon scattering in a two-level mixer
creator: A.V. Vasenin, A.Yu. Dmitriev, S.V. Kadyrmetov, A.N.Bolgar, O.V. Astafiev
description: Abstract A superconducting qubit in a waveguide behaves as a point-like nonlinear element. If irradiated with nearly resonant microwave pulses, the qubit undergoes quantum evolution and generates coherent fields at sideband frequencies due to elastic scattering. This effect is called Quantum Wave Mixing (QWM), and the number of emerged side components depends on the number of interacting photons.

title: Regular black holes with improved energy conditions and their analogues in fluids
creator: Chen Lan, Yan-Gang Miao, Yi-Xiong Zang
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Chen Lan, Yan-Gang Miao, Yi-Xiong Zang. On the premise of the importance of energy conditions for regular black holes, we propose a method to remedy those models that break the dominant energy condition, e.g., the Bardeen and Hayward black holes. We modify the metrics but ensure their regularity at the same time, so that the weak, null, and dominant energy conditions are satisfied, with the exception of the strong energy condition.

title: Reviewer Preferences and Gender Disparities in Aesthetic Judgments Thanks: Citation : Lassen, I.M.S, Bizzoni, Y., Peura, ., Thomsen, R., & Nielbo, K.L. . Reviewer Preferences and Gender Disparities in Aesthetic Judgments. arXiv:xxxx.xxxxx [cs.CY]
creator: Ida Marie S. Lassen, Yuri Bizzoni, Telma Peura, Mads Rosendahl Thomsen, Kristoffer Nielbo
description: Abstract Aesthetic preferences are considered highly subjective resulting in inherently noisy judgements of aesthetic objects, yet certain aspects of aesthetic judgement display convergent trends over time. This paper present a study that uses literary reviews as a proxy for aesthetic judgement in order to identify systematic components that can be attributed to bias.

title: Cyclic changes of the photospheric magnetic field polarity
creator: E. S. Vernova; M. I. Tyasto
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by E. S. Vernova; M. I. Tyasto. The distribution of magnetic fields of positive and negative polarities over the surface of the Sun was studied. Synoptic maps of the photospheric magnetic field (NSO Kitt Peak, 1978–2016) were used for the analysis. In the time-latitude diagram for weak magnetic fields ( B ≤ 5 B\leq 5 G), inclined bands are clearly visible, indicating the alternating dominance of magnetic fields with positive or negative polarity drifting towards the poles of the Sun.

title: Study of entropy production due to electroweak phase transition in Z 2 Z_{2} symmetric extension of the Standard Model
creator: Arnab Chaudhuri, Jaydeb Das
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Arnab Chaudhuri, Jaydeb Das. In this work we consider the simple Z 2 Z_{2} symmetric extension to the Standard Model (SM) and proceed to study the nature of electroweak phase transition (EWPT) in the early universe. We show that the nature of the phase transition changes from a smooth crossover in the SM to a strong first order with this addition of the real scalar. Furthermore, we show the entropy release in this scenario is higher than that of the SM.

title: Statistical and Neural Methods for Cross-lingual Entity Label Mapping in Knowledge Graphs
creator: Gabriel Amaral, Mārcis Pinnis, Inguna Skadiņa, Odinaldo Rodrigues, Elena Simperl
description: Abstract Knowledge bases such as Wikidata amass vast amounts of named entity information, such as multilingual labels, which can be extremely useful for various multilingual and cross-lingual applications. However, such labels are not guaranteed to match across languages from an information consistency standpoint, greatly compromising their usefulness for fields such as machine translation.

title: Ballistic transport of interacting Bose particles in the tight-binding chain
creator: P. S. Muraev 1,2 , D. N. Maksimov 1,3 , and A. R. Kolovsky 1,2
description: Abstract It is known that quantum transport of non-interacting Bose particles across the tight-binding chain is ballistic in the sense that the current does not depend on the chain length. We address the question whether the transport of strongly interacting bosons can be ballistic as well.

title: An Algorithm for the SE(3)-Transformation on Neural Implicit Maps for Remapping Functions
creator: Yijun Yuan, Andreas Nüchter
description: Abstract Implicit representations are widely used for object reconstruction due to their efficiency and flexibility. In 2021, a novel structure named neural implicit map has been invented for incremental reconstruction. A neural implicit map alleviates the problem of inefficient memory cost of previous online 3D dense reconstruction while producing better quality.

title: n − n ′ n-n^{\prime} OSCILLATIONS: SENSITIVITY OF A FIRST UCN BEAM EXPERIMENT
creator: W. SAENZ-AREVALO a {}^{\textrm{a}} on behalf of the collaboration, G. Ban a {}^{\textrm{a}}, J. Chen a {}^{\textrm{a}}, P.-J. Chiu b {}^{\textrm{b}}, B. Clément c {}^{\textrm{c}}, M. Clément c {}^{\textrm{c}}, M. Guigue d {}^{\textrm{d}}, T. Jenke e {}^{\textrm{e}}, P. Larue c {}^{\textrm{c}}, T. Lefort a {}^{\textrm{a}}, O. Nav. Oscillations of the neutron into a hidden sector particle are processes predicted in various Standard Model extensions. This extra channel for neutron disappearance has not been tested experimentally in large portions of the oscillation parameter space.

title: A New Look at the C 0 C^{0} -formulation of the Strong Cosmic Censorship Conjecture
creator: Aditya Iyer, Alexander Y. Yosifov, Vlatko Vedral
description: Abstract We examine the C 0 C^{0} -formulation of the strong cosmic censorship conjecture (SCC) from a quantum complexity-theoretic perspective and argue that for generic black hole parameters as initial conditions for the Einstein equations, corresponding to the expected geometry of a hyperbolic black hole, the metric is C 0 C^{0} -extendable to a larger Lorentzian manifold across the Cauchy

title: CATTO: Just-in-time Test Case Selection and Execution
creator: Dario Amoroso d’Aragona 1 , Fabiano Pecorelli 1 , Simone Romano 2 , Giuseppe Scanniello 2, Maria Teresa Baldassarre 3 , Andrea Janes 4 , Valentina Lenarduzzi 5
description: Abstract Regression testing wants to prevent that errors, which have already been corrected once, creep back into a system that has been updated. A naïve approach consists of re-running the entire test suite (TS) against the changed version of the software under test (SUT). However, this might result in a time- and resource-consuming process; e.g.

title: The ITU Faroese Pairs Dataset
creator: Leon Derczynski, Annika Solveig Hedegaard Isfeldt, Signhild Djurhuus
description: Abstract This article documents a dataset of sentence pairs between Faroese and Danish, produced at ITU Copenhagen. The data covers tranlsation from both source languages, and is intended for use as training data for machine translation systems in this language pair.

title: Crowdsourcing Relative Rankings of Multi-Word Expressions: Experts versus Non-Experts
creator: David Alfter, Therese Lindström Tiedemann, Elena Volodina, [0.5cm] University of Gothenburg University of HelsinkiSpråkbanken Department of Finnish, Finno-UgrianDepartment of Swedish and Scandinavian Studies[0.5cm] david.alfter@gu.setherese.lindstromtiedemann@helsinki.fielena.volodina@gu.se
description: Abstract In this study we investigate to which degree experts and non-experts agree on questions of difficulty in a crowdsourcing experiment. We ask non-experts (second language learners of Swedish) and two groups of experts (teachers of Swedish as a second/foreign language and CEFR experts) to rank multi-word expressions in a crowdsourcing experiment.

title: Efficient WiFi LiDAR SLAM for Autonomous Robots in Large Environments Thanks: K. Ismail, R. Liu, A. Athukorala, B. P. L. Lau, M. Shalihan, C. Yuen, and U-X. Tan are with the Engineering Product Development Pillar, Singapore University of Technology and Design, 8 Somapah Rd, Singapore, 487372. { ran_
creator: Khairuldanial Ismail, Ran Liu, Zhenghong Qin, Achala Athukorala, Billy Pik Lik Lau, Muhammad Shalihan
description: Abstract Autonomous robots operating in indoor and GPS denied environments can use LiDAR for SLAM instead. However, LiDARs do not perform well in geometrically-degraded environments, due to the challenge of loop closure detection and computational load to perform scan matching. Existing WiFi infrastructure can be exploited for localization and mapping with low hardware and computational cost.

title: Robust Information Criterion for Model Selection in Sparse High-Dimensional Linear Regression Models
creator: Prakash B. Gohain, Magnus Jansson
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Prakash B. Gohain, Magnus Jansson. Model selection in linear regression models is a major challenge when dealing with high-dimensional data where the number of available measurements (sample size) is much smaller than the dimension of the parameter space. Traditional methods for model selection such as Akaike information criterion, Bayesian information criterion (BIC) and minimum description length are heavily prone to overfitting in the high-dimensional setting.

title: Meromorphic Solutions of Homogeneous and Non-homogeneous Higher Order Linear Difference Equations in Terms of (p,q)-Order
creator: Subhadip Khan, Chinmay Ghosh, Sanjib Kumar Datta
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Subhadip Khan, Chinmay Ghosh, Sanjib Kumar Datta. In this paper we investigate the growth of meromorphic solutions of homogeneous and non-homogeneous linear difference equations with entire or meromorphic coefficients. We further extend and improve few results on the order of meromorphic solutions by using ( p , q ) − (p,q)- lower order and ( p , q ) − (p,q)- lower type followed by the investigation of Luo and Zheng ( 2016 ) , \left(2016\right), Belaidi and Bellaama ( 2020 ) .

title: A remark on Kashin’s discrepancy argument and partial coloring in the Komlós conjecture
creator: Afonso S. Bandeira, Antoine Maillard, Nikita Zhivotovskiy
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Afonso S. Bandeira, Antoine Maillard, Nikita Zhivotovskiy. In this expository note, we discuss an early partial coloring result of B. Although this result only implies Spencer’s six standard deviations [Trans. Soc., 1985] up to a log ⁡ log ⁡ n \log\log n factor, Kashin’s argument gives a simple proof of the existence of a constant discrepancy partial coloring in the setup of the Komlós conjecture.

title: Detecting Adversarial Examples in Batches - a geometrical approach
creator: Danush Kumar Venkatesh, Peter Steinbach
description: Abstract Many deep learning methods have successfully solved complex tasks in computer vision and speech recognition applications. Nonetheless, the robustness of these models has been found to be vulnerable to perturbed inputs or adversarial examples, which are imperceptible to the human eye, but lead the model to erroneous output decisions.

title: Improved uncertainty quantification for Gaussian process regression based interatomic potentials
creator: Albert P. Bartók, James R. Kermode
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Albert P. Bartók, James R. Kermode. The error estimation capability of machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) based on probabilistic learning methods such as Gaussian process regression (GPR) is currently under-exploited, because of the tendancy of the predicted errors to overestimate the true error. We present approaches based on maximising either the marginal likelihood or an alternative likelihood constructed using leave-one-out cross validation to provide improved error estimates for interatomic potentials based on GPR.

title: Learning Fair Representation via Distributional Contrastive Disentanglement Conference: Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 14–18, 2022; Washington, DC, USA. Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
creator: Changdae Oh, Heeji Won, Junhyuk So, Taero Kim, Yewon Kim, Hosik Choi, Kyungwoo Song
description: Abstract . Learning fair representation is crucial for achieving fairness or debiasing sensitive information. Most existing works rely on adversarial representation learning to inject some invariance into representation. However, adversarial learning methods are known to suffer from relatively unstable training, and this might harm the balance between fairness and predictiveness of representation.

title: Growth of Solutions of Linear Difference Equations with Meromorphic Coefficients in Terms of Iterated p − ϕ p-\phi Order
creator: Anirban Bandyopadhyay, Chinmay Ghosh, Sanjib Kumar Datta
description: Abstract In this article we have studied complex linear homogeneous difference equations where the coefficients are meromorphic functions, having finite iterated p − ϕ p-\phi order. We have made some estimations on the growth of its nontrivial solutions. Also we have extended some of the previous results of Zhou-Zheng (2017), Belaïdi-Benkarouba (2019) and Belaïdi-Bellaama (2021).

title: Generalised Policy Improvement with Geometric Policy Composition
creator: Shantanu Thakoor, Mark Rowland, Diana Borsa, Will Dabney, Rémi Munos, André Barreto
description: Abstract We introduce a method for policy improvement that interpolates between the greedy approach of value-based reinforcement learning (RL) and the full planning approach typical of model-based RL. The new method builds on the concept of a geometric horizon model (GHM, also known as a γ \gamma -model), which models the discounted state-visitation distribution of a given policy.

title: Information Geometry of Risks and Returns Original version 9 June 2022. Journal-ref: Risk, June (2023).
creator: Andrei N. Soklakov
description: Abstract We reveal a geometric structure underlying both hedging and investment products. The structure follows from a simple formula expressing investment risks in terms of returns. This informs optimal product designs. Optimal pure hedging (including cost-optimal products) and hybrid hedging (where a partial hedge is built into an optimal investment product) are considered.

title: From a few Accurate 2D Correspondences to 3D Point Clouds
description: Abstract Key points, correspondences, projection matrices, point clouds and dense clouds are the skeletons in image-based 3D reconstruction, of which point clouds have the important role in generating a realistic and natural model for a 3D reconstructed object. To achieve a good 3D reconstruction, the point clouds must be almost everywhere in the surface of the object.

title: Beyond Ridge Regression for Distribution-Free Data
creator: Koby Bibas, Meir Feder
description: Abstract In supervised batch learning, the predictive normalized maximum likelihood (pNML) has been proposed as the min-max regret solution for the distribution-free setting, where no distributional assumptions are made on the data. However, the pNML is not defined for a large capacity hypothesis class as over-parameterized linear regression.

title: Compositional Exploration of Combinatorial Scientific Models
creator: Kristopher Brown, Tyler Hanks, James Fairbanks
description: Abstract We implement a novel representation of model search spaces as diagrams over a category of models, where we have restricted attention to a broad class of models whose structure is presented by 𝒞 \mathcal{C} -sets. (Co)limits in these diagram categories allow the creation of composite model spaces from more primitive spaces.

title: Solving small-scale clustering problems in approximate lightcone mocks 2022 Solving small-scale clustering problems in approximate lightcone mocks – References
creator: Alex Smith, Shaun Cole, Cameron Grove, Peder Norberg, Pauline Zarrouk
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alex Smith, Shaun Cole, Cameron Grove, Peder Norberg, Pauline Zarrouk. Realistic lightcone mocks are important in the clustering analyses of large galaxy surveys. For simulations where only the snapshots are available, it is common to create approximate lightcones by joining together the snapshots in spherical shells. We assess the two-point clustering measurements of central galaxies in approximate lightcones built from the Millennium-XXL simulation, which are constructed using different numbers of snapshots.

title: C-Pack of IPAs : A C90 Program Benchmark of Introductory Programming Assignments CCS: Applied computing Computer-assisted instruction CCS: Theory of computation Program semantics CCS: Theory of computation Program analysis CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning CCS: Theory of computation Prog
creator: Pedro Orvalho, Mikoláš Janota, Vasco Manquinho
description: Abstract . Due to the vast number of students enrolled in Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs), there has been an increasing number of automated program repair techniques focused on introductory programming assignments ( IPAs ). Such techniques take advantage of previous correct student implementations in order to provide automated, comprehensive, and personalized feedback to students.

title: Tensor-on-Tensor Regression: Riemannian Optimization, Over-parameterization, Statistical-computational Gap, and Their Interplay
description: Abstract We study the tensor-on-tensor regression, where the goal is to connect tensor responses to tensor covariates with a low Tucker rank parameter tensor/matrix without prior knowledge of its intrinsic rank. We propose the Riemannian gradient descent (RGD) and Riemannian Gauss-Newton (RGN) methods and cope with the challenge of unknown rank by studying the effect of rank over-parameterization.

title: Testing chiral unitary models for the Λ ⁡ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) in K + ​ π ​ Σ K^{+}\pi\Sigma photoproduction
creator: P. C. Bruns, A. Cieplý, M. Mai
description: Abstract We adopt a novel formalism for the low-energy analysis of the γ ​ p → K + ​ π ​ Σ \gamma p\to K^{+}\pi\Sigma photoproduction reaction to calculate the π ​ Σ \pi\Sigma invariant mass distributions in the Λ ⁡ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) resonance region.

title: Mass-energy equivalence in gravitationally bound quantum states of the neutron
creator: Germain Tobar, Simon Haine, Fabio Costa, Magdalena Zych
description: Abstract Gravitationally bound neutrons have become an important tool in the experimental searches for new physics, such as modifications to Newton’s force or candidates for dark matter particles. Here we include the relativistic effects of mass-energy equivalence into the model of gravitationally bound neutrons.

title: Spectral-Efficiency of Cell-Free Massive MIMO with Multicarrier-Division Duplex
creator: Bohan Li, Lie-Liang Yang, Fellow, IEEE, Robert G. Maunder, Senior Member, IEEE, Songlin Sun, Senior Member, IEEE, Pei Xiao, Senior Member, IEEE
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Bohan Li, Lie-Liang Yang, Fellow, IEEE, Robert G. Maunder, Senior Member, IEEE, Songlin Sun, Senior Member, IEEE, Pei Xiao, Senior Member, IEEE. A multicarrier-division duplex (MDD)-based cell-free (CF) scheme, namely MDD-CF, is proposed, which enables downlink (DL) data and uplink (UL) data or pilots to be concurrently transmitted on mutually orthogonal subcarriers in distributed CF massive MIMO (mMIMO) systems.

title: Sign-changing blow-up for the Yamabe equation at the lowest energy level Thanks: The first author was supported by the FNRS CdR grant J.0135.19, the Fonds Thélam and an ARC Avancé 2020 grant. The second author was supported by the Discovery Grant RGPIN-2016-04195 from the Natural Sciences and Engine
creator: Bruno Premoselli, Jérôme Vétois
description: Abstract . We investigate the blow-up behavior of sequences of sign-changing solutions for the Yamabe equation on a Riemannian manifold ( M , g ) (M,g) of positive Yamabe type. For each dimension n ≥ 11 n\geq 11 , we describe the value of the minimal energy threshold at which blow-up occurs.

title: An explicit Plancherel formula for line bundles over the one-sheeted hyperboloid
creator: Frederik Bang–Jensen & Jonathan Ditlevsen
description: Abstract . In this paper we consider G = SL ⁡ ( 2 , ℝ ) G=\SL(2,\mathbb{R}) and H H the subgroup of diagonal matrices. Then X = G / H X=G/H is a unimodular homogeneous space which can be identified with the one-sheeted hyperboloid.

title: Dead ends on wreath products and lamplighter groups
creator: Eduardo Silva
description: Abstract . For any finite group A A and any finitely generated group B B , we prove that the corresponding lamplighter group A ≀ B A\wr B admits a standard generating set with unbounded depth, and that if B B is abelian then the above is true for every standard generating set.

title: Discovery of the Content and Engagement with the Content
creator: Pushkal Agarwal, Nishanth Sastry, Edward Wood
description: Abstract Introduction For much of the 20th century, British politicians bemoaned the decline in reporting of Parliament by the press. The UK Parliament’s Modernisation Committee noted ruefully in 2004 that ‘‘the House can no longer expect to receive a certain amount of media coverage as of right.

title: Spherical Sliced-Wasserstein
creator: Clément Bonet, Paul Berg, Nicolas Courty, François Septier, Lucas Drumetz, Minh-Tan Pham, Université Bretagne Sud, LMBA, IRISA; IMT Atlantique, Lab-STICC {clement.bonet, paul.berg, francois.septier}@univ-ubs.fr{nicolas.courty, minh-tan.pham}@irisa.fr ; lucas.drumetz@imt-atlantique.fr
description: Abstract Many variants of the Wasserstein distance have been introduced to reduce its original computational burden. In particular the Sliced-Wasserstein distance (SW), which leverages one-dimensional projections for which a closed-form solution of the Wasserstein distance is available, has received a lot of interest.

title: Leveraging Uncertainty in Deep Learning for Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma Grading
creator: Biraja Ghoshal Bhargab Ghoshal, Allan Tucker
description: Abstract Pancreatic cancers have one of the worst prognoses compared to other cancers, as they are diagnosed when cancer has progressed towards its latter stages. The current manual histological grading for diagnosing pancreatic adenocarcinomas is time-consuming and often results in misdiagnosis.

title: The Importance of Background Information for Out of Distribution Generalization
creator: Jupinder Parmar, Khaled Saab, Brian Pogatchnik, Daniel Rubin, Christopher Ré
description: Abstract Domain generalization in medical image classification is an important problem for trustworthy machine learning to be deployed in healthcare. We find that existing approaches for domain generalization which utilize ground-truth abnormality segmentations to control feature attributions have poor out-of-distribution (OOD) performance relative to the standard baseline of empirical risk minimization (ERM).

title: Reinforcement Learning for Economic Policy: A New Frontier?
creator: Callum Rhys Tilbury
description: Abstract Agent-based computational economics is a field with a rich academic history, yet one which has struggled to enter mainstream policy design toolboxes—plagued by the challenges associated with representing a complex and dynamic reality. The field of Reinforcement Learning (RL), too, has a rich history, and has recently been at the centre of several exponential developments.

title: Self-supervised speech unit discovery from articulatory and acoustic features using VQ-VAE
creator: Marc-Antoine Georges, Jean-Luc Schwartz, Thomas Hueber
description: Abstract The human perception system is often assumed to recruit motor knowledge when processing auditory speech inputs. Using articulatory modeling and deep learning, this study examines how this articulatory information can be used for discovering speech units in a self-supervised setting. We used vector-quantized variational autoencoders (VQ-VAE) to learn discrete representations from articulatory and acoustic speech data.

title: Quantum Zeno Repeaters
creator: Veysel Bayrakci, Fatih Ozaydin
description: Abstract Quantum repeaters pave the way for long-distance quantum communications and quantum Internet, and the idea of quantum repeaters is based on entanglement swapping which requires the implementation of controlled quantum gates. Frequently measuring a quantum system affects its dynamics which is known as the quantum Zeno effect (QZE).

title: A Human-Centric Method for Generating Causal Explanations in Natural Language for Autonomous Vehicle Motion Planning
creator: Balint Gyevnar, Massimiliano Tamborski, Cheng Wang, Christopher G. Lucas, Shay B. Cohen, Stefano V. Albrecht
description: Abstract Inscrutable AI systems are difficult to trust, especially if they operate in safety-critical settings like autonomous driving. Therefore, there is a need to build transparent and queryable systems to increase trust levels. We propose a transparent, human-centric explanation generation method for autonomous vehicle motion planning and prediction based on an existing white-box system called IGP2.

title: Open-Sampling: Exploring Out-of-Distribution Data for Re-balancing Long-tailed Datasets
creator: Hongxin Wei, Lue Tao, Renchunzi Xie, Lei Feng, Bo An
description: Abstract Deep neural networks usually perform poorly when the training dataset suffers from extreme class imbalance . Recent studies found that directly training with out-of-distribution data (i.e., open-set samples) in a semi-supervised manner would harm the generalization performance. In this work, we theoretically show that out-of-distribution data can still be leveraged to augment the minority classes from a Bayesian perspective.

title: Open Source Variational Quantum Eigensolver Extension of the Quantum Learning Machine (QLM) for Quantum Chemistry Publication type: RESEARCH ARTICLE
creator: Mohammad Haidar*, Marko J. Rančić, Thomas Ayral, Yvon Maday, Jean-Philip Piquemal*, M. Haidar, M. J. Rančić, T. Ayral, Y. Maday, J-P. Piquemal
description: Abstract Quantum Chemistry (QC) is one of the most promising applications of Quantum Computing. However, present quantum processing units (QPUs) are still subject to large errors. Therefore, noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware is limited in terms of qubit counts/circuit depths. Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) algorithms can potentially overcome such issues. Here, we introduce the OpenVQE open-source QC package.

title: A general error analysis for randomized low-rank approximation methods Thanks:
creator: Youssef Diouane, Selime Gürol, Alexandre Scotto di Perrotolo, Xavier Vasseur
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Youssef Diouane, Selime Gürol, Alexandre Scotto di Perrotolo, Xavier Vasseur. We propose a general error analysis related to the low-rank approximation of a given real matrix in both the spectral and Frobenius norms. First, we derive deterministic error bounds that hold with some minimal assumptions. Second, we derive error bounds in expectation in the non-standard Gaussian case, assuming a non-trivial mean and a general covariance matrix for the random matrix variable.

title: Local Characteristic Decomposition Based Central-Upwind Scheme Thanks: Institute of Mathematics, University of Mainz, Germany; lukacova@uni-mainz.de
creator: Alina Chertock, Shaoshuai Chu, Michael Herty, Alexander Kurganov
description: Abstract We propose novel less diffusive schemes for conservative one- and two-dimensional hyperbolic systems of nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs). The main challenges in the development of accurate and robust numerical methods for the studied systems come from the complicated wave structures, such as shocks, rarefactions and contact discontinuities, arising even for smooth initial conditions.

title: Abstract
creator: A compact complex Hermitian manifold
description: Abstract A Calabi-Yau theorem for Vaisman manifolds Liviu Ornea 1 1 1 Liviu Ornea is partially supported by Romanian Ministry of Education and Research, Program PN-III, Project number PN-III-P4-ID-PCE-2020-0025, Contract 30/04.02.2021 , Misha Verbitsky 2 2 2 Misha Verbitsky is partially supported by the HSE University Basic Research Program, FAPERJ E-26/202.912/2018 and CNPq - Process 313608/2017-2.

title: Complexity of the Multiobjective Spanner Problem
creator: Fritz Bökler, Henning Jasper
description: Abstract In this paper, we take an in-depth look at the complexity of a hitherto unexplored Multiobjective Spanner (MSp) problem. The MSp is a multiobjective generalization of the well-studied Minimum t-Spanner problem. This multiobjective approach allows us to find solutions that offer a viable compromise between cost and utility.

title: Observation of 𝜼 𝒄 ​ ( 𝟐 ​ 𝑺 ) → 𝟑 ​ ( 𝝅 + ​ 𝝅 − ) \eta_{c}(2S)\rightarrow 3(\pi^{+}\pi^{-}) and measurements of 𝝌 𝒄 ​ 𝑱 → 𝟑 ​ ( 𝝅 + ​ 𝝅 − ) \chi_{cJ}\rightarrow 3(\pi^{+}\pi^{-}) in 𝝍 ⁡ ( 𝟑𝟔𝟖𝟔 ) \psi(3686) radiative transitions
creator: M. Ablikim 1 , M. N. Achasov 11,b , P. Adlarson 70 , M. Albrecht 4 , R. Aliberti 31 , A. Amoroso 69A,69C , M. R. An 35 , Q. An 66,53 , X. H. Bai 61 , Y. Bai 52 , O. Bakina 32 , R. Baldini Ferroli 26A , I. Balossino 1,27A , Y. Ban 42,g , V. Batozskaya 1,40 , D. Becker 31 , K. Begzsuren 29 , N. Berger
description: Abstract The hadronic decay η c ​ ( 2 ​ S ) → 3 ​ ( π + ​ π − ) \eta_{c}(2S)\rightarrow 3(\pi^{+}\pi^{-}) is observed with a statistical significance of 9.3 standard deviations using ( 448.1 ± 2.9 ) × 10 6 (448.1\pm 2.

title: A Closed Universe: de Sitter Cosmic Gate
creator: S. Danial Forghani, S. Habib Mazharimousavi
description: Abstract A new cosmological object in analogy with the concept of a wormhole in general relativity is introduced. As wormholes connect two distant points through a tunnel in a spacetime, this new object connects two spacetime through a large mouth which is referred to as a ”Cosmic Gate”.

title: Species Distribution Modeling with Expert Elicitation and Bayesian Calibration
creator: Karel Kaurila, Sanna Kuningas, Antti Lappalainen, Jarno Vanhatalo
description: Abstract Species distribution models (SDMs) are key tools in ecology, conservation and management of natural resources. They are commonly trained by scientific survey data but, since surveys are expensive, there is a need for complementary sources of information to train them.

title: Universality of the number variance in rotational invariant two-dimensional Coulomb gases Thanks: The work of Gernot Akemann was partly funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) grant SFB 1283/2 2021 – 317210226. Sung-Soo Byun was partially supported by Samsung Science and Technology Found
creator: Gernot Akemann, Sung-Soo Byun, Markus Ebke
description: Abstract . An exact map was established by Lacroix-A-Chez-Toine, Majumdar, and Schehr in [ 45 ] between the N N complex eigenvalues of complex non-Hermitian random matrices from the Ginibre ensemble, and the positions of N N non-interacting Fermions in a rotating trap in the ground state.

title: FedNew: A Communication-Efficient and Privacy-Preserving Newton-Type Method for Federated Learning Thanks: Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur, India. Thanks: University of Oulu Thanks: School of Industrial Engineering and School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Purdue University, USA.
creator: Anis Elgabli, Chaouki Ben Issaid, Amrit S. Bedi
description: Abstract Newton-type methods are popular in federated learning due to their fast convergence. Still, they suffer from two main issues, namely: low communication efficiency and low privacy due to the requirement of sending Hessian information from clients to parameter server (PS).

title: Exploring Web3 From the View of Blockchain
creator: Qin Wang ⋆, Rujia Li, Qi Wang, Shiping Chen, Mark Ryan, Thomas Hardjono
description: Abstract Web3 is the most hyped concept from 2020 to date, greatly motivating the prosperity of the Internet of Value and Metaverse. However, no solid evidence stipulates the exact definition, criterion, or standard in the sense of such a buzzword. To fill the gap, we aim to clarify the term in this work.

title: Decentralized adaptive clustering of deep nets is beneficial for client collaboration
creator: Edvin Listo Zec, Ebba Ekblom, Martin Willbo, Olof Mogren, Sarunas Girdzijauskas
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Edvin Listo Zec, Ebba Ekblom, Martin Willbo, Olof Mogren, Sarunas Girdzijauskas. We study the problem of training personalized deep learning models in a decentralized peer-to-peer setting, focusing on the setting where data distributions differ between the clients and where different clients have different local learning tasks. We study both covariate and label shift, and our contribution is an algorithm which for each client finds beneficial collaborations based on a similarity estimate for the local task.

title: Entity-Graph Enhanced Cross-Modal Pretraining for Instance-level Product Retrieval
creator: Xiao Dong*, Xunlin Zhan*, Yunchao Wei, Xiaoyong Wei, Yaowei Wang, Minlong Lu, Xiaochun Cao, and, Xiaodan Liang
description: Abstract Our goal in this research is to study a more realistic environment in which we can conduct weakly-supervised multi-modal instance-level product retrieval for fine-grained product categories. We first contribute the Product1M datasets, and define two real practical instance-level retrieval tasks to enable the evaluations on the price comparison and personalized recommendations.

title: Channel-wise Mixed-precision Assignment for DNN Inference on Constrained Edge Nodes
creator: Matteo Risso 2 , Alessio Burrello 1 , Luca Benini 1 , Enrico Macii 3 , Massimo Poncino 2 , Daniele Jahier Pagliari 2
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Matteo Risso 2 , Alessio Burrello 1 , Luca Benini 1 , Enrico Macii 3 , Massimo Poncino 2 , Daniele Jahier Pagliari 2. Quantization is widely employed in both cloud and edge systems to reduce the memory occupation, latency, and energy consumption of deep neural networks.

title: Optimal tests of genuine multipartite nonlocality
creator: Mahasweta Pandit, Artur Barasiński, István Márton, Tamás Vértesi, Wiesław Laskowski
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Mahasweta Pandit, Artur Barasiński, István Márton, Tamás Vértesi, Wiesław Laskowski. We propose an optimal numerical test for genuine multipartite nonlocality based on linear programming. In particular, we consider two non-equivalent models of local hidden variables, namely the Svetlichny and the no-signaling bilocal model.

title: On the Bug-proneness of Structures Inspired by Functional Programming in JavaScript Projects
creator: Fernando Alves 1 , Delano Oliveira 1 , Fernanda Madeiral 2 , and Fernando Castor 3
description: Abstract Language constructs inspired by functional programming have made their way into most mainstream programming languages. Many researchers and developers consider that these constructs lead to programs that are more concise, reusable, and easier to understand. Notwithstanding, few studies investigate the prevalence of these structures and the implications of using them in mainstream programming languages.

title: Moment Generating Stirling Numbers and Applications
creator: Ludwig Frank
description: Abstract Abstract. In this paper, we investigate certain combinatorial numbers, the moment generating Stirling numbers . They are a special case of Hsu’s generalized Stirling numbers and satisfy many more properties and combinatorial identities than are known in the general case.

title: MineDojo : Building Open-Ended Embodied Agents with Internet-Scale Knowledge
creator: Linxi Fan, Guanzhi Wang, Yunfan Jiang, Ajay Mandlekar, Yuncong Yang, Haoyi Zhu, Andrew Tang, De-An Huang, Yuke Zhu, Anima Anandkumar
description: Abstract Autonomous agents have made great strides in specialist domains like Atari games and Go. However, they typically learn tabula rasa in isolated environments with limited and manually conceived objectives, thus failing to generalize across a wide spectrum of tasks and capabilities.

title: SMPL: Simulated Industrial Manufacturing and Process Control Learning Environments
creator: Mohan Zhang, Xiaozhou Wang, Benjamin Decardi-Nelson, Song Bo, An Zhang, Jinfeng Liu, Sile Tao, Jiayi Cheng, Xiaohong Liu, DengDeng Yu, Matthew Poon, Animesh Garg
description: Abstract Traditional biological and pharmaceutical manufacturing plants are controlled by human workers or pre-defined thresholds. Modernized factories have advanced process control algorithms such as model predictive control (MPC). However, there is little exploration of applying deep reinforcement learning to control manufacturing plants. One of the reasons is the lack of high fidelity simulations and standard APIs for benchmarking.

title: Asymmetric transport computations in Dirac models of topological insulators
creator: Guillaume Bal, Jeremy G Hoskins, Zhongjian Wang
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Guillaume Bal, Jeremy G Hoskins, Zhongjian Wang. This paper presents a fast algorithm for computing transport properties of two-dimensional Dirac operators with linear domain walls, which model the macroscopic behavior of the robust and asymmetric transport observed at an interface separating two two-dimensional topological insulators. Our method is based on reformulating the partial differential equation as a corresponding volume integral equation, which we solve via a spectral discretization scheme.

title: Epsilon-regularity for the Brakke flow with boundary
creator: Carlo Gasparetto
description: Abstract We prove that, if a Brakke flow with boundary is close enough to a stationary half-plane with density one, then it is C 1 , α C^{1,\alpha} . Our approach is based on viscosity techniques introduced by Savin in the context of elliptic equations.

title: Sparsity of Graphs that Allow Two Distinct Eigenvalues
creator: Wayne Barrett, Shaun Fallat, Veronika Furst, Franklin Kenter, Shahla Nasserasr, Brendan Rooney, Michael Tait, Hein van der Holst
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Wayne Barrett, Shaun Fallat, Veronika Furst, Franklin Kenter, Shahla Nasserasr, Brendan Rooney, Michael Tait, Hein van der Holst. The parameter q ⁡ ( G ) q(G) of a graph G G is the minimum number of distinct eigenvalues over the family of symmetric matrices described by G G .

title: The image of polynomials and Waring type problems on upper triangular matrix algebras
creator: Saikat Panja, Sachchidanand Prasad
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Saikat Panja, Sachchidanand Prasad. Let p p be a polynomial in non-commutative variables x 1 , x 2 , … , x n x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{n} with constant term zero over an algebraically closed field K K . The object of study in this paper is the image of this kind of polynomial over the algebra of upper triangular matrices T m ​ ( K ) T_{m}(K) .

title: Faraday effect of light caused by plane gravitational wave
creator: Andrey A. Shoom
description: Abstract Gravitational field can cause a rotation of polarisation plane of light. This phenomenon is known as the gravitational Faraday effect. We study the gravitational Faraday effect of linearly polarised light propagating in the gravitational field of a weak plane gravitational wave (GW) with “ + + ”, “ × \times ”, and elliptical polarisation modes.

title: The Pixel Luminosity Telescope: A detector for luminosity measurement at CMS using silicon pixel sensors
creator: The CMS BRIL Collaboration
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by The CMS BRIL Collaboration. The Pixel Luminosity Telescope is a silicon pixel detector dedicated to luminosity measurement at the CMS experiment at the LHC. It is located approximately 1.75 \unit m from the interaction point and arranged into 16 “telescopes”, with eight telescopes installed around the beam pipe at either end of the detector and each telescope composed of three individual silicon sensor planes.

title: Distances for Comparing Multisets and Sequences
creator: George Bolt, Simón Lunagómez, Christopher Nemeth
description: Abstract Measuring the distance between data points is fundamental to many statistical techniques, such as dimension reduction or clustering algorithms. However, improvements in data collection technologies has led to a growing versatility of structured data for which standard distance measures are inapplicable.

title: Interior point methods are not worse than Simplex This project has received funding from the European Research Council (ERC) under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme: DD from grant agreement no. 805241-QIP, BN and LAV from grant agreements no. 757481-ScaleOpt. We tha
creator: Xavier Allamigeon, Daniel Dadush, Georg Loho, Bento Natura, László A. Végh
description: Abstract We develop a new ‘subspace layered least squares’ interior point method (IPM) for solving linear programs. Applied to an n n -variable linear program in standard form, the iteration complexity of our IPM is up to an O ⁡ ( n 1.5 ​ log ⁡ n ) O(n^{1.

title: How Robust is Unsupervised Representation Learning to Distribution Shift?
creator: Yuge Shi, Imant Daunhawer & Julia E. Vogt, Philip H.S. Torr, Amartya Sanyal
description: Abstract The robustness of machine learning algorithms to distributions shift is primarily discussed in the context of supervised learning (SL) . As such, there is a lack of insight on the robustness of the representations learned from unsupervised methods, such as self-supervised learning (SSL) and auto-encoder based algorithms (AE) , to distribution shift.

title: Correlators of Four Light-Ray Operators in CCFT
creator: Shounak De, Yangrui Hu, Akshay Yelleshpur Srikant, Anastasia Volovich
description: Abstract Building on results in arXiv:2203.04255, we compute the correlator of four gluon light-ray operators in celestial CFT. We find that it is described by Fox H-functions and generalized I-functions of multiple variables. We also analyze light-ray correlators for a scalar amplitude involving the exchange of a massive scalar.

title: BUDDI-MaNGA I: A statistical sample of cleanly decomposed bulge and disc spectra 2022 BUDDI-MaNGA I: A statistical sample of cleanly decomposed bulge and disc spectra – 14
creator: Evelyn J. Johnston, Boris Häußler, & Keerthana Jegatheesan
description: Abstract Many galaxies display clear bulges and discs, and understanding how these components form is a vital step towards understanding how the galaxy has evolved into what we see today. The BUDDI-MaNGA project aims to study galaxy evolution and morphological transformations through the star-formation histories of the bulges and discs.

title: BUDDI-MaNGA II: The Star-Formation Histories of Bulges and Discs of S0s 2022 BUDDI-MaNGA II: The Star-Formation Histories of Bulges and Discs of S0s – References
creator: Evelyn J. Johnston, Boris Häußler, Keerthana Jegatheesan, Amelia Fraser-McKelvie, Lodovico Coccato, Ariana Cortesi, Yara Jaffé, Gaspar Galaz, Marcelo Mora & Yasna Ordenes-Briceño
description: Abstract Many processes have been proposed to explain the quenching of star formation in spiral galaxies and their transformation into S0s. These processes affect the bulge and disc in different ways, and so by isolating the bulge and disc spectra, we can look for these characteristic signatures.

title: Logic-based Reward Shaping for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
creator: Ingy ElSayed-Aly, Lu Feng
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ingy ElSayed-Aly, Lu Feng. Reinforcement learning (RL) relies heavily on exploration to learn from its environment and maximize observed rewards. Therefore, it is essential to design a reward function that guarantees optimal learning from the received experience. Previous work has combined automata and logic based reward shaping with environment assumptions to provide an automatic mechanism to synthesize the reward function based on the task. However, there is limited work on how to expand logic-based reward shaping to Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL).

title: Edge-Aided Sensor Data Sharing in Vehicular Communication Networks Thanks: This work was supported by the German Federal Ministry of Transport and Digital Infrastructure (BMVI) in the project “KIVI – KI im Verkehr Ingolstadt” and the Bavarian Ministry of Economic Affairs, Regional Development and En
creator: Rui Song 1 2 , Anupama Hegde 3 , Numan Senel 4 , Alois Knoll 2 , Andreas Festag 1 3
description: Abstract Sensor data sharing in vehicular networks can significantly improve the range and accuracy of environmental perception for connected automated vehicles. Different concepts and schemes for dissemination and fusion of sensor data have been developed. It is common to these schemes that measurement errors of the sensors impair the perception quality and can result in road traffic accidents.

title: Incorporating intratumoral heterogeneity into weakly-supervised deep learning models via variance pooling
creator: Iain Carmichael, Andrew H. Song *, Richard J. Chen, Drew F.K. Williamson, Tiffany Y. Chen, Faisal Mahmood
description: Abstract Supervised learning tasks such as cancer survival prediction from gigapixel whole slide images (WSIs) are a critical challenge in computational pathology that requires modeling complex features of the tumor microenvironment. These learning tasks are often solved with deep multi-instance learning (MIL) models that do not explicitly capture intratumoral heterogeneity.

title: Continuous cohomology of gauge algebras and bornological Loday-Quillen-Tsygan theorems
creator: Lukas Miaskiwskyi
description: Abstract . We investigate the well-known Loday-Quillen-Tsygan theorem, which calculates the Lie algebra homology of the general linear algebra 𝔤 ​ 𝔩 ⁡ ( A ) \gl(A) for an associative algebra A A in terms of cyclic homology, and extend the proof to bornological Lie algebra homology of Fréchet and LF-algebras. For Fréchet spaces, this equals continuous Lie algebra homology.

title: Learning to self-fold at a bifurcation
creator: Chukwunonso Arinze 1 , Menachem Stern 2 , Sidney R. Nagel 1 , Arvind Murugan 1
description: Abstract Disordered mechanical systems can deform along a network of pathways that branch and recombine at special configurations called bifurcation points. Multiple pathways are accessible from these bifurcation points; consequently, computer-aided design algorithms have been sought to achieve a specific structure of pathways at bifurcations by rationally designing the geometry and material properties of these systems.

title: CtrlFormer: Learning Transferable State Representation for Visual Control via Transformer
creator: Yao Mu, Shoufa Chen, Mingyu Ding, Jianyu Chen, Runjian Chen, Ping Luo
description: Abstract Transformer has achieved great successes in learning vision and language representation, which is general across various downstream tasks. In visual control, learning transferable state representation that can transfer between different control tasks is important to reduce the training sample size. However, porting Transformer to sample-efficient visual control remains a challenging and unsolved problem.

title: Characteristics of Interference in Licensed and Unlicensed Bands for Intelligent Spectrum Management
creator: Zhuoran Su, Kaveh Pahlavan
description: Abstract The exponential growth of IoT devices and the demand of smart devices for higher data rates has heightened the need for sharing and managing spectrum resources in cellular 5G/6G operating in licensed bands and Wi-Fi technologies operating in unlicensed bands. Intelligent spectrum management has emerged as a key concept in dynamic spectrum allocation.

title: Loss-driven topological transitions in lasing
creator: Grazia Salerno, Rebecca Heilmann, Kristian Arjas, Kerttu Aronen, Jani-Petri Martikainen, Päivi Törmä
description: Abstract We experimentally observe lasing in a hexamer plasmonic lattice and find that when tuning the scale of the unit cell, the polarization properties of the emission change. By a theoretical analysis we identify the lasing modes as quasi bound states in continuum (quasi-BICs) of topological charges of zero, one or two.

title: Colonoscopy 3D video dataset with paired depth from 2D-3D registration Journal: Medical Image Analysis
creator: Taylor L. Bobrow, Mayank Golhar, Rohan Vijayan, Venkata S. Akshintala, Juan R. Garcia, Nicholas J. Durr
description: Abstract Screening colonoscopy is an important clinical application for several 3D computer vision techniques, including depth estimation, surface reconstruction, and missing region detection. However, the development, evaluation, and comparison of these techniques in real colonoscopy videos remain largely qualitative due to the difficulty of acquiring ground truth data.

title: Scaling multi-species occupancy models to large citizen science datasets
creator: Martin Ingram, Damjan Vukcevic, Nick Golding
description: Abstract keywords Variational inference, hierarchical models, species distribution models, Bayesian statistics 1. Citizen science datasets can be very large and promise to improve species distribution modelling, but detection is imperfect, risking bias when fitting models. In particular, observers may not detect species that are actually present.

title: Mass-Zero constrained dynamics for simulations based on orbital-free density functional theory
creator: A. Coretti, T. Baird, R. Vuilleumier, S. Bonella
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by A. Coretti, T. Baird, R. Vuilleumier, S. Bonella. A new algorithm for efficient and fully time-reversible integration of first-principles molecular dynamics based on orbital-free density functional theory (OFDFT) is presented. The algorithm adapts to this nontrivial case the recently introduced Mass-Zero (MaZe) constrained dynamics. The formalism ensures that full adiabatic separation is enforced between nuclear and electronic degrees of freedom and, consequently, that the exact Born-Oppenheimer probability for the nuclei is sampled. Numerical integration of the MaZe dynamics combines standard molecular dynamics algorithms, e.g.

title: niksss at HinglishEval: Language-agnostic BERT-based Contextual Embeddings with Catboost for Quality Evaluation of the Low-Resource Synthetically Generated Code-Mixed Hinglish Text
creator: Nikhil Singh
description: Abstract This paper describes the system description for the HinglishEval challenge at INLG 2022. The goal of this task was to investigate the factors influencing the quality of the code-mixed text generation system. The task was divided into two subtasks, quality rating prediction and annotators’ disagreement prediction of the synthetic Hinglish dataset.

title: Popular decision tree algorithms are provably noise tolerant
creator: Guy Blanc, Jane Lange, Ali Malik, Li-Yang Tan
description: Abstract Using the framework of boosting, we prove that all impurity-based decision tree learning algorithms, including the classic ID3, C4.5, and CART, are highly noise tolerant. Our guarantees hold under the strongest noise model of nasty noise, and we provide near-matching upper and lower bounds on the allowable noise rate.

title: Graphs with Sudoku number n − 1 n-1
creator: Alexey Pokrovskiy
description: Abstract Recently Lau-Jeyaseeli-Shiu-Arumugam introduced the concept of the “Sudoku colourings” of graphs — partial χ ⁡ ( G ) \chi(G) -colourings of G G that have a unique extension to a proper χ ⁡ ( G ) \chi(G) -colouring of all the vertices.

title: Quantum Simulation of ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} Lattice Gauge theory with minimal resources
creator: Reinis Irmejs, Mari-Carmen Banuls, J. Ignacio Cirac
description: Abstract The quantum simulation of fermionic gauge field theories is one of the anticipated uses of quantum computers in the NISQ era. Recently work has been done to simulate properties of the fermionic ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} gauge field theory in (1+1) D and the pure gauge theory in (2+1) D.

title: Simulations for the Q Q statistic with constant and inverse variance weights for binary effect measures
creator: Elena Kulinskaya, David C. Hoaglin
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Elena Kulinskaya, David C. Hoaglin. \vskip-12.0pt Cochran’s Q Q statistic is routinely used for testing heterogeneity in meta-analysis. Its expected value (under an incorrect null distribution) is part of several popular estimators of the between-study variance, τ 2 \tau^{2} .
