description: Abstract Let λ 𝕂 ​ ( m ) \lambda_{\mathbb{K}}(m) denote the maximal absolute projection constant over the subspaces of dimension m m . Apart from the trivial case for m = 1 m=1 , the only known value of λ 𝕂 ​ ( m ) \lambda_{\mathbb{K}}(m) is for m = 2 m=2 and 𝕂 = ℝ . \mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}.

title: Floquet engineering of titled and gapped Dirac materials
creator: Andrii Iurov 1 , Liubov Zhemchuzhna 1,2 , Godfrey Gumbs 2,3 , Danhong Huang 4,5 , Kathy Blaise 1 and Chinedu Ejiogu 1
description: Abstract We have established a rigorous theoretical formalism for Floquet engineering, or investigating and eventually tailoring most crucial electronic properties of tetragonal molybdenum disulfide (1T ′ -MoS 2 ), by applying an external high-frequency dressing field in the off-resonant regime.

title: Video frame interpolation for high dynamic range sequences captured with dual-exposure sensors Volume: 42 Issue: 2
creator: Uğur Çoğalan, Mojtaba Bemana, Hans-Peter Seidel and Karol Myszkowski Max-Planck-Institut für Informatik, Germany
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Uğur Çoğalan, Mojtaba Bemana, Hans-Peter Seidel and Karol Myszkowski Max-Planck-Institut für Informatik, Germany. Video frame interpolation (VFI) enables many important applications such as slow motion playback and frame rate conversion. However, one major challenge in using VFI is accurately handling high dynamic range (HDR) scenes with complex motion. To this end, we explore the possible advantages of dual-exposure sensors that readily provide sharp short and blurry long exposures that are spatially registered and whose ends are temporally aligned.

title: 3D Object Detection for Autonomous Driving: A Comprehensive Survey Publication type: generic article
creator: Jiageng Mao 1, Shaoshuai Shi 3, Xiaogang Wang 1,2, Hongsheng Li 1,2
description: Abstract Autonomous driving, in recent years, has been receiving increasing attention for its potential to relieve drivers’ burdens and improve the safety of driving. In modern autonomous driving pipelines, the perception system is an indispensable component, aiming to accurately estimate the status of surrounding environments and provide reliable observations for prediction and planning.

title: Interval groups related to finite Coxeter groups Part II
creator: Barbara Baumeister, Derek F. Holt, Georges Neaime, Sarah Rees
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Barbara Baumeister, Derek F. Holt, Georges Neaime, Sarah Rees. We provide a complete description of the presentations of the interval groups related to quasi-Coxeter elements in finite Coxeter groups. In the simply laced cases, we show that each interval group is the quotient of the Artin group associated with the corresponding Carter diagram by the normal closure of a set of twisted cycle commutators, one for each 4-cycle of the diagram.

title: Fast Krasnosel’skiĭ-Mann algorithm with a convergence rate of the fixed point iteration of o ⁡ ( 1 k ) o\left(\frac{1}{k}\right) Thanks: Received by the editors June 21, 2022; accepted for publication (in revised form) August 22, 2023;
creator: Radu Ioan Boţ, Dang-Khoa Nguyen
description: Abstract The Krasnosel’skiĭ-Mann (KM) algorithm is the most fundamental iterative scheme designed to find a fixed point of an averaged operator in the framework of a real Hilbert space, since it lies at the heart of various numerical algorithms for solving monotone inclusions and convex optimization problems.

title: On Function of Evolution of Distribution for Time Homogeneous Markov Processes
creator: Tomasz R. Bielecki, Jacek Jakubowski, Maciej Wiśniewolski
description: Abstract A study of time homogeneous, real valued Markov processes with a special property and a non-atomic initial distribution is provided. The new notion of a function of evolution of distribution which determines the dependency between one dimensional distributions of a process is introduced.

title: Bounds and extremal graphs for total dominating identifying codes
creator: Florent Foucaud, Tuomo Lehtilä
description: Abstract An identifying code C C of a graph G G is a dominating set of G G such that any two distinct vertices of G G have distinct closed neighbourhoods within C C . The smallest size of an identifying code of G G is denoted γ ID ​ ( G ) \gamma^{\text{\tiny{ID}}}(G) .

title: Two-Hop Age of Information Scheduling for Multi-UAV Assisted Mobile Edge Computing: FRL vs MADDPG
creator: Marjan Tajik, Mohammadreza Maleki, Nader Mokari, , Mohammad Reza Javan, , Hamid Saeedi , , Bile Peng, , and Eduard A. Jorswieck
description: Abstract In this work, we adopt the emerging technology of mobile edge computing (MEC) in the Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) for communication-computing systems, to optimize the age of information (AoI) in the network. We assume that tasks are processed jointly on UAVs and BS to enhance edge performance with limited connectivity and computing.

title: Bisecting horn angles
creator: Sergiy Koshkin
description: Abstract A horn angle between a circle and its tangent is considered in Euclid’s Elements , and Euclid remarks that it is smaller than any acute rectilinear angle. Already in antiquity, Proclus wondered whether it is possible to bisect horn angles.

title: Non-classical linear divisibility sequences and cyclotomic polynomials
creator: Sergiy Koshkin
description: Abstract Divisibility sequences are defined by the property that their elements divide each other whenever their indices do. The divisibility sequences that also satisfy a linear recurrence, like the Fibonacci numbers, are generated by polynomials that divide their compositions with every positive integer power.

title: The analytic extension of solutions to initial-boundary value problems outside their domain of definition
creator: Matthew Farkas, Jorge Cisneros, Bernard Deconinck
description: Abstract We examine the analytic extension of solutions of linear, constant-coefficient initial-boundary value problems outside their spatial domain of definition. We use the Unified Transform Method or Method of Fokas, which gives a representation for solutions to half-line and finite-interval initial-boundary value problems as integrals of kernels with explicit spatial and temporal dependence.

title: The Power of Regularization in Solving Extensive-Form Games
creator: Mingyang Liu, Asuman Ozdaglar, Tiancheng Yu, Kaiqing Zhang
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Mingyang Liu, Asuman Ozdaglar, Tiancheng Yu, Kaiqing Zhang. In this paper, we investigate the power of regularization , a common technique in reinforcement learning and optimization, in solving extensive-form games (EFGs). We propose a series of new algorithms based on regularizing the payoff functions of the game, and establish a set of convergence results that strictly improve over the existing ones, with either weaker assumptions or stronger convergence guarantees.

title: Unbiased Teacher v2: Semi-supervised Object Detection for Anchor-free and Anchor-based Detectors
creator: Yen-Cheng Liu, Chih-Yao Ma, Zsolt Kira
description: Abstract With the recent development of Semi-Supervised Object Detection (SS-OD) techniques, object detectors can be improved by using a limited amount of labeled data and abundant unlabeled data. However, there are still two challenges that are not addressed: (1) there is no prior SS-OD work on anchor-free detectors, and (2) prior works are ineffective when pseudo-labeling bounding box regression.

title: DoG-HiT: A novel VLBI Multiscale Imaging Approach
creator: H.Müller, A.P. Lobanov
description: Abstract Context. Reconstructing images from very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) data with sparse sampling of the Fourier domain ( uv -coverage) constitutes an ill-posed deconvolution problem. It requires application of robust algorithms maximizing the information extraction from all of the sampled spatial scales and minimizing the influence of the unsampled scales on image quality. Aims.

title: Rapid Viscoelastic Spreading
creator: Ambre Bouillant, Pim J. Dekker, Michiel A. Hack, Jacco H. Snoeijer
description: Abstract We investigate the rapid spreading dynamics of a viscoelastic drop on a solid. Upon contact, surface tension drives a fast motion of the contact line along the substrate. Here, we resolve this motion for viscoelastic liquids by experiments on aqueous polymer solutions of varying concentration.

title: AdS/BCFT correspondence and BTZ black hole within electric field
creator: Fabiano F. Santos a
description: Abstract This paper, presents the gravity duals of Conformal Field Theories with boundaries. This theory is known as AdS/BCFT correspondence. In this duality, our system has 3D gravity coupling with the Maxwell field dual to 2D BCFT. On the gravity side, we consider a 3D BTZ black hole.

title: Log-GPIS-MOP: A Unified Representation for Mapping, Odometry and Planning
creator: Lan Wu, Ki Myung Brian Lee, Cedric Le Gentil, Teresa Vidal-Calleja
description: Abstract Whereas dedicated scene representations are required for each different task in conventional robotic systems, this paper demonstrates that a unified representation can be used directly for multiple key tasks. We propose the Log-Gaussian Process Implicit Surface for Mapping, Odometry and Planning (Log-GPIS-MOP): a probabilistic framework for surface reconstruction, localisation and navigation based on a unified representation.

title: Caustics of light rays and Euler’s angle of inclination
creator: Sergiy Koshkin*, Ivan Rocha
description: Abstract Euler used intrinsic equations expressing the radius of curvature as a function of the angle of inclination to find curves similar to their evolutes. We interpret the evolute of a plane curve optically, as the caustic (envelope) of light rays normal to it, and study the Euler’s problem for general caustics.

title: C ∗ C^{*} -algebra Net: A New Approach Generalizing Neural Network Parameters to C ∗ C^{*} -algebra
creator: Yuka Hashimoto, Zhao Wang, Tomoko Matsui
description: Abstract We propose a new framework that generalizes the parameters of neural network models to C ∗ C^{*} -algebra-valued ones. C ∗ C^{*} -algebra is a generalization of the space of complex numbers. A typical example is the space of continuous functions on a compact space.

title: Highly excited and exotic fully-strange tetraquark states Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
creator: Rui-Rui Dong t1, Niu Su t1, Hua-Xing Chen e1
description: Abstract Some hadrons have the exotic quantum numbers that the traditional q ¯ ​ q \bar{q}q mesons and q ​ q ​ q qqq baryons can not reach, such as J P ​ C = 0 − ⁣ − / 0 + ⁣ − / 1 − ⁣ + / 2 + ⁣ − / 3 − ⁣ + /

title: The Fallacy of AI Functionality Conference: 2022 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency; June 21–24, 2022; Seoul, Republic of Korea 2022 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT ’22), June 21–24, 2022, Seoul, Republic of Korea Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.114
creator: Inioluwa Deborah Raji*, I. Elizabeth Kumar*, Aaron Horowitz, Andrew D. Selbst
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Inioluwa Deborah Raji*, I. Elizabeth Kumar*, Aaron Horowitz, Andrew D. Selbst. Deployed AI systems often do not work. They can be constructed haphazardly, deployed indiscriminately, and promoted deceptively. However, despite this reality, scholars, the press, and policymakers pay too little attention to functionality. This leads to technical and policy solutions focused on “ethical” or value-aligned deployments, often skipping over the prior question of whether a given system functions, or provides any benefits at all.

title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
creator: Sean T. Vittadello 1,2 & Michael P.H. Stumpf 1,2,3
description: Abstract Biology is data-rich, and it is equally rich in concepts and hypotheses. Part of trying to understand biological processes and systems is therefore to confront our ideas and hypotheses with data using statistical methods to determine the extent to which our hypotheses agree with reality.

title: Integrability of Kerr-Newman spacetime with cloud strings, quintessence and electromagnetic field
creator: Wenfu Cao 1,2, Wenfang Liu 1, Xin Wu 1,2,3
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Wenfu Cao 1,2, Wenfang Liu 1, Xin Wu 1,2,3. The dynamics of charged particles moving around a Kerr-Newman black hole surrounded by cloud strings, quintessence and electromagnetic field is integrable due to the presence of a fourth constant of motion like the Carter constant. The fourth motion constant and the axial-symmetry of the spacetime give a chance to the existence of radial effective potentials with stable circular orbits in two-dimensional planes, such as the equatorial plane and other nonequatorial planes.

title: ILX: Intelligent "Location+X" Data Systems (Vision Paper) CCS: Information systems Database design and models CCS: Information systems Location based services CCS: Information systems Geographic information systems CCS: Information systems Database management system engines CCS: Information systems
creator: Walid G. Aref 1 , Ahmed M. Aly 2 , Anas Daghistani 3 , Yeasir Rayhan 1 , Jianguo Wang 1 , Libin Zhou 1
description: Abstract . Due to the ubiquity of mobile phones and location-detection devices, location data is being generated in very large volumes. Queries and operations that are performed on location data warrant the use of database systems. Despite that, location data is being supported in data systems as an afterthought.

title: Towards Trustworthy Edge Intelligence: Insights from Voice-Activated Services
creator: Wiebke Toussaint Hutiri, Aaron Yi Ding
description: Abstract In an age of surveillance capitalism, anchoring the design of emerging smart services in trustworthiness is urgent and important. Edge Intelligence, which brings together the fields of AI and Edge computing, is a key enabling technology for smart services. Trustworthy Edge Intelligence should thus be a priority research concern.

title: Temporal Link Prediction via Adjusted Sigmoid Function and 2-Simplex Sructure
creator: Ruizhi Zhang, Qiaozi Wang, Qiming Yang, Wei Wei
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ruizhi Zhang, Qiaozi Wang, Qiming Yang, Wei Wei. Temporal network link prediction is an important task in the field of network science, and has a wide range of applications in practical scenarios. Revealing the evolutionary mechanism of the network is essential for link prediction, and how to effectively utilize the historical information for temporal links and efficiently extract the high-order patterns of network structure remains a vital challenge.

title: Multiple Testing Framework for Out-of-Distribution Detection
creator: Akshayaa Magesh, Venugopal V. Veeravalli, Anirban Roy, Susmit Jha
description: Abstract We study the problem of Out-of-Distribution (OOD) detection, that is, detecting whether a Machine Learning (ML) model’s output can be trusted at inference time. While a number of tests for OOD detection have been proposed in prior work, a formal framework for studying this problem is lacking.

title: Hands-on Wireless Sensing with Wi-Fi: A Tutorial
creator: Zheng Yang, Yi Zhang, Guoxuan Chi, Guidong Zhang
description: Abstract . With the rapid development of wireless communication technology, wireless access points (AP) and internet of things (IoT) devices have been widely deployed in our surroundings. Various types of wireless signals (e.g., Wi-Fi, LoRa, LTE) are filling out our living and working spaces.

title: Characterizing Human Actions in the Digital Platform by Temporal Context
creator: Akira Matsui, Emilio Ferrara
description: Abstract Recent advances in digital platforms generate rich, high‑dimensional logs of human behavior, and machine learning models have helped social scientists explain knowledge accumulation, communication, and information diffusion. Such models, however, almost always treat behavior as sequences of actions, abstracting the inter‑temporal information among actions.

title: The eROSITA Final Equatorial-Depth Survey (eFEDS)
creator: N. Ota, N. T. Nguyen-Dang, I. Mitsuishi, M. Oguri, M. Klein, N. Okabe, M. E. Ramos-Ceja, T. H. Reiprich, F. Pacaud, E. Bulbul, M. Brüggen, A. Liu, K. Migkas, I. Chiu, V. Ghirardini, S. Grandis, Y.-T. Lin, H. Miyatake, S. Miyazaki, J. S. Sanders
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by N. Ota, N. T. Nguyen-Dang, I. Mitsuishi, M. Oguri, M. Klein, N. Okabe, M. E. Ramos-Ceja, T. H. Reiprich, F. Pacaud, E. Bulbul, M. Brüggen, A. Liu, K. Migkas, I. Chiu, V. Ghirardini, S. Grandis, Y.-T. Lin, H. Miyatake, S. Miyazaki, J. S. Sanders. We present the results of a systematic X-ray analysis of optically rich galaxy clusters detected by the Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) survey in the eROSITA Final Equatorial-Depth Survey (eFEDS) field.

title: Conjugate point criteria on the area-preserving diffeomorphism group
creator: Stephen C. Preston
description: Abstract This paper answers some questions about conjugate points along the geodesics corresponding to steady 2D Euler flows, posed by a paper of Drivas-Misiołek-Shi-Yoneda. We present a new sufficient criterion for the existence of conjugate points, which improves on the criterion of Misiołek.

title: Chiral current in Floquet cavity-magnonics
creator: Shi-fan Qi, Jun Jing
description: Abstract Floquet engineering can induce complex collective behaviour and interesting synthetic gauge-field in quantum systems through temporal modulation of system parameters by periodic drives. Using a Floquet drive on frequencies of the magnon modes, we realize a chiral state-transfer in a cavity-magnonic system. The time-reversal symmetry is broken in such a promising platform for coherent information processing.

title: DualCoOp: Fast Adaptation to Multi-Label Recognition with Limited Annotations
creator: Ximeng Sun Ping Hu Kate Saenko
description: Abstract Solving multi-label recognition (MLR) for images in the low-label regime is a challenging task with many real-world applications. Recent work learns an alignment between textual and visual spaces to compensate for insufficient image labels, but loses accuracy because of the limited amount of available MLR annotations.

title: Cooperative Edge Caching via Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning in Fog Radio Access Networks
creator: Qi Chang 1 , Yanxiang Jiang 1,2,∗ , Fu-Chun Zheng 1,2 , Mehdi Bennis 3 , and Xiaohu You 1
description: Abstract In this paper, the cooperative edge caching problem in fog radio access networks (F-RANs) is investigated. To minimize the content transmission delay, we formulate the cooperative caching optimization problem to find the globally optimal caching strategy.By considering the non-deterministic polynomial hard (NP-hard) property of this problem, a Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL)-based cooperative caching scheme is proposed.

title: Dynamic Message Propagation Network for RGB-D Salient Object Detection
creator: Baian Chen, Zhilei Chen, Xiaowei Hu, Jun Xu, Haoran Xie, Mingqiang Wei, Jing Qin
description: Abstract This paper presents a novel deep neural network framework for RGB-D salient object detection by controlling the message passing between the RGB images and depth maps on the feature level and exploring the long-range semantic contexts and geometric information on both RGB and depth features to infer salient objects.

title: Harmonic Oscillators of Mathematical Biology: Many Faces of a Predator-Prey Model
creator: Sergiy Koshkin*, Isaiah Meyers
description: Abstract We show that a number of models in virus dynamics, epidemiology and plant biology can be presented as “damped” versions of the Lotka-Volterra predator-prey model, by analogy to the damped harmonic oscillator. The analogy deepens with the use of Lyapunov functions, which allow us to characterize their dynamics and even make some estimates.

title: A hypergraph Heilmann–Lieb theorem Thanks: Corresponding author. Yi Wang Thanks: Funding. Supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (No. 12171002)
creator: Jiang-Chao Wan, Yi Wang, Yi-Zheng Fan
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jiang-Chao Wan, Yi Wang, Yi-Zheng Fan. The Heilmann–Lieb theorem is a fundamental theorem in algebraic combinatorics which provides a characterization of the distribution of the zeros of matching polynomials of graphs. In this paper, we establish a hypergraph Heilmann–Lieb theorem as follows. Let ℋ \mathcal{H} be a connected k k -graph with maximum degree Δ ≥ 2 {\Delta}\geq 2 and let μ ⁡ ( ℋ , x ) \mu(\mathcal{H},x) be its matching polynomial.

title: Policy Optimization with Linear Temporal Logic Constraints
creator: Cameron Voloshin, Hoang M. Le, Swarat Chaudhuri, Yisong Yue
description: Abstract We study the problem of policy optimization (PO) with linear temporal logic (LTL) constraints. The language of LTL allows flexible description of tasks that may be unnatural to encode as a scalar cost function. We consider LTL-constrained PO as a systematic framework, decoupling task specification from policy selection, and as an alternative to the standard of cost shaping.

title: Single-Qubit Reaped Quantum State Tomography
creator: Mahn-Soo Choi
description: Abstract Quantum state tomography is the experimental procedure of determining an unknown state. It is not only essential for the verification of resources and processors of quantum information but is also important in its own right with regard to the foundation of quantum mechanics.

title: Guardian Angel: A Novel Walking Aid for the Visually Impaired DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: ; August 08–11, 2022; Vancouver, BC, Canada Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 CCS: Human-centered computing Human computer interaction (HCI)
creator: Ko-Wei Tai, HuaYen Lee, Hsin-Huei Chen, Jeng-Sheng Yeh, Ming Ouhyoung
description: Abstract . This work introduces Guardian Angel, an Android App that assists visually impaired people to avoid danger in complex traffic environment. The system, consisting of object detection by pre-trained YOLO model, distance estimation and moving direction estimation, provides information about surrounding vehicles and alarms users of potential danger without expensive special purpose device.

title: Retardation effect and dark state in a waveguide QED setup with rectangle cross section
creator: Yang Xue, Zhihai Wang
description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the dynamics of a two-atom system which couples to a quasi-one dimensional waveguide with rectangle cross section. The waveguide supports different TM and TE modes and the former ones play as environment by on-demand choosing the dipole moment of the atoms. Such environment induces the interaction and collective dissipation of the atoms.

title: Shuffle Gaussian Mechanism for Differential Privacy
creator: Seng Pei Liew, Tsubasa Takahashi
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Seng Pei Liew, Tsubasa Takahashi. We study Gaussian mechanism in the shuffle model of differential privacy (DP). Particularly, we characterize the mechanism’s Rényi differential privacy (RDP), showing that it is of the form: ϵ ⁡ ( λ ) ≤ 1 λ − 1 ​ log ⁡ ( e − λ / 2 σ 2 n λ ​ ∑ k 1 + … + k n = λ ; k 1 , … , k n ≥ 0 ( λ k 1 , … ,

title: Monolithic parabolic regularization of the MHD equations and entropy principles Note: This research is funded by Swedish Research Council (VR) under grant number 2021-04620.
creator: Tuan Anh Dao, Murtazo Nazarov
description: Abstract We show at the PDE level that the monolithic parabolic regularization of the equations of ideal magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) is compatible with all the generalized entropies, fulfills the minimum entropy principle, and preserves the positivity of density and internal energy.

title: RAiSE: simulation-based analytical model of AGN jets and lobes 2022 RAiSE: simulation-based analytical model of AGN jets and lobes – References
creator: Ross J. Turner, Patrick M. Yates-Jones, Stanislav S. Shabala, Benjamin Quici and, Georgia S. C. Stewart
description: Abstract We present an analytical model for the evolution of extended active galactic nuclei (AGNs) throughout their full lifecycle, including the initial jet expansion, lobe formation, and eventual remnant phases. A particular focus of our contribution is on the early jet expansion phase, which is traditionally not well captured in analytical models.

title: C-SENN: Contrastive Self-Explaining Neural Network
creator: Yoshihide Sawada, Keigo Namamura
description: Abstract In this study, we use a self-explaining neural network (SENN), which learns unsupervised concepts, to acquire concepts that are easy for people to understand automatically. In concept learning, the hidden layer retains verbalizable features relevant to the output, which is crucial when adapting to real-world environments where explanations are required.

title: Scalable Distributed Algorithms for Size-Constrained Submodular Maximization in the MapReduce and Adaptive Complexity Models
creator: Yixin Chen chen777@tamu.edu, Tonmoy Dey tdey@fsu.edu, Alan Kuhnle kuhnle@tamu.edu
description: Abstract Distributed maximization of a submodular function in the MapReduce (MR) model has received much attention, culminating in two frameworks that allow a centralized algorithm to be run in the MR setting without loss of approximation, as long as the centralized algorithm satisfies a certain consistency property – which had previously only been known to be satisfied by the standard

title: Higher energy modes of Fractional quantum Hall Effect
creator: Debashis Das, Moumita Indra, Dwipesh Majumder
description: Abstract We have calculated the energy spectra for almost all the filling fraction in the Jain series, low energy fundamental mode as well as higher energy modes using CF theory. The nature of low energy mode and higher energy mode is nearly identical roton mode.

title: Swinging a playground swing Torque controls for inducing sustained oscillations
creator: Sergiy Koshkin, Vojin Jovanovic
description: Abstract Models of a playground swing have been studied since the 1960s. However, in most of them, the position of the swinger is controlled directly. This simplifies the problem but hides the mechanics of torques applied to keep the swing moving in a regular pattern. This article studies these mechanics.

title: Dipper Donkin Quantized Matrix Algebra and Reflection Equation Algebra at root of unity
creator: Snehashis Mukherjee 1 and Sanu Bera 2
description: Abstract . In this article the quantized matrix algebras as in the title have been studied at a root of unity. A full classification of simple modules over such quantized matrix algebras of rank 2 2 along with a class of finite dimensional indecomposable modules are given. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 16D60, 16T20, 16S36, 16R20 1.

title: Rebalance and Smear for Multi-jet Background Estimation
creator: Christian Sander
description: Abstract For many particle collider searches for physics beyond the Standard Model in final states with jets and missing transverse momentum, events from QCD multi-jet processes are an important and challenging background contribution. The CMS and ATLAS experiments have previously developed data-driven methods designed to succeed where Monte Carlo methods suffer large theoretical and experimental uncertainties.

title: 5th Place Solution for YouTube-VOS Challenge 2022: Video Object Segmentation
creator: Wangwang Yang*, Jinming Su*, Yiting Duan, Tingyi Guo and Junfeng Luo Vision Intelligence Department (VID), Meituan {yangwangwang, sujinming, duanyiting, guotingyi, luojunfeng}@meituan.com
description: Abstract Video object segmentation (VOS) has made significant progress with the rise of deep learning. However, there still exist some thorny problems, for example, similar objects are easily confused and tiny objects are difficult to be found. To solve these problems and further improve the performance of VOS, we propose a simple yet effective solution for this task.

title: Domain-Adaptive Text Classification with Structured Knowledge from Unlabeled Data
creator: Tian LiPeking University davidli@pku.edu.cn, Xiang ChenPeking University caspar@pku.edu.cn Zhen DongUniversity of California, Berkeley zhendong@berkeley.edu Weijiang YuSun Yat-sen University weijiangyu8@gmail.com Yijun YanUniversity of California, Berkeley bunnyyan@berkeley.edu Kurt KeutzerUniversit
description: Abstract Domain adaptive text classification is a challenging problem for the large-scale pretrained language models because they often require expensive additional labeled data to adapt to new domains. Existing works usually fails to leverage the implicit relationships among words across domains.

title: From Multi-agent to Multi-robot: A Scalable Training and Evaluation Platform for Multi-robot Reinforcement Learning
creator: Zhiuxan Liang, Jiannong Cao, Fellow, IEEE, Shan Jiang, Divya Saxena, Jinlin Chen, Huafeng Xu
description: Abstract Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has been gaining extensive attention from academia and industries in the past few decades. One of the fundamental problems in MARL is how to evaluate different approaches comprehensively. Most existing MARL methods are evaluated in either video games or simplistic simulated scenarios. It remains unknown how these methods perform in real-world scenarios, especially multi-robot systems.

title: Distortion-Aware Network Pruning and Feature Reuse for Real-time Video Segmentation
creator: Hyunsu Rhee, Dongchan Min, Sunil Hwang, Bruno Andreis, Sung Ju Hwang
description: Abstract Real-time video segmentation is a crucial task for many real-world applications such as autonomous driving and robot control. Since state-of-the-art semantic segmentation models are often too heavy for real-time applications despite their impressive performance, researchers have proposed lightweight architectures with speed-accuracy trade-offs, achieving real-time speed at the expense of reduced accuracy.

title: SPBERTQA: A Two-Stage Question Answering System Based on Sentence Transformers for Medical Texts
creator: Nhung Thi-Hong Nguyen, Phuong Phan-Dieu Ha, Luan Thanh Nguyen, Kiet Van Nguyen, Ngan Luu-Thuy Nguyen
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Nhung Thi-Hong Nguyen, Phuong Phan-Dieu Ha, Luan Thanh Nguyen, Kiet Van Nguyen, Ngan Luu-Thuy Nguyen. Question answering (QA) systems have gained explosive attention in recent years. However, QA tasks in Vietnamese do not have many datasets. Significantly, there is mostly no dataset in the medical domain.

title: NLOS Ranging Mitigation with Neural Network Model for UWB Localization
creator: Muhammad Shalihan, Ran Liu, Chau Yuen
description: Abstract Localization of robots is vital for navigation and path planning, such as in cases where a map of the environment is needed. Ultra-Wideband (UWB) for indoor location systems has been gaining popularity over the years with the introduction of low-cost UWB modules providing centimetre-level accuracy.

title: Gorenstein cohomological dimension and stable categories for groups Thanks: E-mail: wren @ \char 64\relax cqnu.edu.cn
creator: Wei Ren
description: Abstract . First we study the Gorenstein cohomological dimension Gcd R ​ G {\rm Gcd}_{R}G of groups G G over coefficient rings R R , under changes of groups and rings; a characterization for finiteness of Gcd R ​ G {\rm Gcd}_{R}G is given.

title: Density of periodic measures and large deviation principle for generalized ( α , β \alpha,\beta )- transformations
creator: Mao Shinoda, Kenichiro Yamamoto
description: Abstract . We introduce generalized ( α , β ) (\alpha,\beta) -transformations, which include all ( α , β ) (\alpha,\beta) and generalized β \beta -transformations, and prove that all transitive generalized ( α , β ) (\alpha,\beta) -transformations satisfy the level-2 large deviation principle with a unique measure of maximal entropy.

title: Crucial role of vibrational entropy in the Si ( 111 ) (111) - 7 × 7 7\times 7 surface structure stability
creator: R. A. Zhachuk, J. Coutinho
description: Abstract We investigate the relative thermodynamic stability of the 3 × 3 3\times 3 , 5 × 5 5\times 5 , 7 × 7 7\times 7 , 9 × 9 9\times 9 and infinitely large structures related to the dimers-adatoms-stacking faults family of Si ( 111 ) (111) surface reconstructions by means of first-principles calculations.

title: Occultation Portal: a web-based platform for data collection and analysis of stellar occultations 2022 Occultation Portal: a web-based platform for data collection and analysis of stellar occultations – 12
creator: Y. Kilic , F. Braga-Ribas , M. Kaplan , O. Erece , D. Souami , M. Dindar , J. Desmars , B. Sicardy , B. E. Morgado , M. N. Shameoni , F. L. Rommel , and A. R. Gomes-Júnior
description: Abstract Recording a stellar occultation is one powerful method that gives direct information about the physical properties of the occulting solar system object. In order to obtain reliable and accurate results, simultaneous observations from different locations across-track of the projected path are of great importance.

title: Degeneracy in epilepsy: Multiple Routes to Hyperexcitable Brain Circuits and their Repair
description: Abstract Tristan Manfred Stöber a , Danylo Batulin a , Jochen Triesch a,1 , Rishikesh Narayanan b,1 , Peter Jedlicka a,c,d,1,* a Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies, 60438 Frankfurt am Main, Germany b Cellular Neurophysiology Laboratory, Molecular Biophysics Unit, Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore 560012, India c ICAR3R – Interdisciplinary Centre for 3Rs in Animal Research, Faculty of Medicine, Justus

title: Asymptotic Nash Equilibrium for the M M -ary Sequential Adversarial Hypothesis Testing Game This work was presented in part at the 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory (ISIT) in Espoo, Finland.
creator: Jiachun Pan ∗ , Yonglong Li ∗ , Vincent Y. F. Tan ∗,†
description: Abstract In this paper, we consider a novel M M -ary sequential hypothesis testing problem in which an adversary is present and perturbs the distributions of the samples before the decision maker observes them. This problem is formulated as a sequential adversarial hypothesis testing game played between the decision maker and the adversary.

title: Analyzing Büchi Automata with Graph Neural Networks
creator: Christophe Stammet, Prisca Dotti, Ulrich Ultes-Nitsche, Andreas Fischer
description: Abstract Büchi Automata on infinite words present many interesting problems and are used frequently in program verification and model checking. A lot of these problems on Büchi automata are computationally hard, raising the question if a learning-based data-driven analysis might be more efficient than using traditional algorithms.

title: An improved method for estimating the velocity field of coronal propagating disturbances
creator: Huw Morgan 1, Marianna Korsos 1
description: Abstract keywords Image processing, Corona \setlastpage \inarticletrue {opening} 1 Introduction Morgan and Hutton 2018 present a method called Time Normalised Optical Flow (TNOF), which revealed the presence of propagating disturbances (PD) across broad regions of the corona, including part of a small active region and quiet Sun.

title: Diversified Adversarial Attacks based on Conjugate Gradient Method
creator: Keiichiro Yamamura, Haruki Sato, Nariaki Tateiwa, Nozomi Hata, Toru Mitsutake, Issa Oe, Hiroki Ishikura, Katsuki Fujisawa
description: Abstract Deep learning models are vulnerable to adversarial examples, and adversarial attacks used to generate such examples have attracted considerable research interest. Although existing methods based on the steepest descent have achieved high attack success rates, ill-conditioned problems occasionally reduce their performance.

title: Page curve and symmetries
creator: Pak Hang Chris Lau, Toshifumi Noumi, Yuhei Takii, Kotaro Tamaoka
description: Abstract Motivated by the quantum process of black hole evaporation and its implications for symmetries, we consider a qubit system with a random dynamics as a toy model of black hole. We compute its symmetry-resolved entropies and discuss its implications. We first consider the case where charges are conserved and compute the symmetry-resolved entropies.

title: Extensions of Yang-Baxter sets
creator: Valeriy G. Bardakov, Dmitry V. Talalaev
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Valeriy G. Bardakov, Dmitry V. Talalaev. The paper extends the notion of braided set and its close relative - the Yang-Baxter set – to the category of vector spaces and explore structure aspects of such a notion as morphisms and extensions.

title: Brown representability for triangulated categories with a linear action by a graded ring Thanks: Partly supported by the NSF grant DMS-1700985, and the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation in the framework of an Alexander von Humboldt Professorship endowed by the German Federal Ministry of Education an
creator: Janina C. Letz
description: Abstract . In this paper we give necessary and sufficient conditions for a functor to be representable in a strongly generated triangulated category which has a linear action by a graded ring, and we discuss some applications and examples. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 18G80 1.

title: Two-Photon Interference LiDAR Imaging Journal: osajournal Publication type: Research Article
creator: Robbie Murray, \authormark 1 and Ashley Lyons \authormark 1,*
description: Abstract Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) is a key 3D imaging technology that provides micron scale depth resolution for bio-imaging. This resolution substantially surpasses what it typically achieved in Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) which is often limited to the millimetre scale due to the impulse response of the detection electronics.

title: On approximating the rank of graph divisors
creator: Kristóf Bérczi, Hung P. Hoang, Lilla Tóthmérész
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kristóf Bérczi, Hung P. Hoang, Lilla Tóthmérész. Baker and Norine initiated the study of graph divisors as a graph-theoretic analogue of the Riemann-Roch theory for Riemann surfaces. One of the key concepts of graph divisor theory is the rank of a divisor on a graph.

title: Dual unitary circuits in random geometries
creator: Yusuf Kasim & Tomaž Prosen
description: Abstract Recently introduced dual unitary brickwork circuits have been recognised as paradigmatic exactly solvable quantum chaotic many-body systems with tunable degree of ergodicity and mixing. Here we show that regularity of the circuit lattice is not crucial for exact solvability.

title: Benchmarking Constraint Inference in Inverse Reinforcement Learning
creator: Guiliang Liu, Yudong Luo, Ashish Gaurav, Kasra Rezaee, Pascal Poupart
description: Abstract When deploying Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents into a physical system, we must ensure that these agents are well aware of the underlying constraints. In many real-world problems, however, the constraints are often hard to specify mathematically and unknown to the RL agents. To tackle these issues, Inverse Constrained Reinforcement Learning (ICRL) empirically estimates constraints from expert demonstrations.

title: Extending the flux homomorphism to volume-preserving homeomorphisms
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by . This paper extends the flux homomorphism to volume-preserving homeomorphisms. A surprising ( C 0 , δ ) − (C^{0},\delta)- rigidity result where the extended flux groups coincide with the standard flux group is proved. The introduced tools, which also include a Poincaré duality with Fathi’s mass flow and a norm on the group of volume-preserving homeomorphisms, indicate a potential for new flexibility in the behavior of homeomorphisms.

title: Parameter Estimation Methods of Required Rate of Return on Stock
creator: Battulga Gankhuu
description: Abstract In this study, we introduce new estimation methods for the required rate of return of the stochastic dividend discount model (DDM) and the private company valuation model, which will appear below. To estimate the required rate of return, we use the maximum likelihood method, the Bayesian method, and the Kalman filtering.

title: Two results of n n -exangulated categories † † footnotetext: Jian He was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (Grant No. 12171230). Panyue Zhou was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (Grant No. 11901190).
creator: Jian He, Jing He, Panyue Zhou
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jian He, Jing He, Panyue Zhou. n n -exangulated categories were introduced by Herschend-Liu-Nakaoka which are a simultaneous generalization of n n -exact categories and ( n + 2 ) (n+2) -angulated categories. This paper consists of two results on n n -exangulated categories: (1) we give an equivalent characterization of the axiom (EA2); (2) we provide a new way to construct a closed subfunctor of an n n -exangulated category.

title: Studying the role of named entities for content preservation in text style transfer
creator: Nikolay Babakov 1, David Dale 1, Varvara Logacheva 1, Irina Krotova 2, Alexander Panchenko 1
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Nikolay Babakov 1, David Dale 1, Varvara Logacheva 1, Irina Krotova 2, Alexander Panchenko 1. Text style transfer techniques are gaining popularity in Natural Language Processing, finding various applications such as text detoxification, sentiment, or formality transfer. However, the majority of the existing approaches were tested on such domains as online communications on public platforms, music, or entertainment yet none of them were applied to the domains which are typical for task-oriented production systems, such as personal plans arrangements (e.g.

creator: Yuchen Jiang, Qi Li, Han Zhu, Jinbei Yu, Jin Li, Ziru Xu, Huihui Dong, Bo Zheng
description: Abstract . Industrial recommender systems usually hold data from multiple business scenarios and are expected to provide recommendation services for these scenarios simultaneously. In the retrieval step, the topK high-quality items selected from a large number of corpus usually need to be various for multiple scenarios.

title: Euclidean Steiner Spanners: Light and Sparse
creator: Sujoy Bhore, Csaba D. Tóth
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sujoy Bhore, Csaba D. Tóth. Lightness and sparsity are two natural parameters for Euclidean ( 1 + ε ) (1+\varepsilon) -spanners. Classical results show that, when the dimension d ∈ ℕ d\in\mathbb{N} and ε > 0 \varepsilon>0 are constant, every set S S of n n points in d d -space admits an ( 1 + ε ) (1+\varepsilon) -spanners with O ⁡ ( n ) O(n) edges and weight proportional to that of the Euclidean MST of S S .

title: \SOUL@setup \SOUL@ Misspelling Semantics in Thai
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by . User-generated content is full of misspellings. Rather than being just random noise, we hypothesise that many misspellings contain hidden semantics that can be leveraged for language understanding tasks. This paper presents a fine-grained annotated corpus of misspelling in Thai, together with an analysis of misspelling intention and its possible semantics to get a better understanding of the misspelling patterns observed in the corpus.

title: The Log Private Company Valuation Model
creator: Battulga Gankhuu
description: Abstract For a public company, pricing and hedging models of options and equity–linked life insurance products have been sufficiently developed. However, for a private company, because of unobserved prices, pricing and hedging models of the European options and life insurance products are in their early stages of development.

title: Threshold transient growth as a criterion for turbulent mean profiles
creator: Vilda K. Markeviciute 1, Rich R. Kerswell 1
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Vilda K. Markeviciute 1, Rich R. Kerswell 1. Lozano-Duran et al ( J. , 914 , A8, 2021) have recently identified the ability of streamwise-averaged turbulent streak fields 𝒰 ⁡ ( y , z , t ) ​ 𝒙 ^ {\cal U}(y,z,t)\hat{\mbox{\boldmath$x$}} in minimal channels to produce short-term transient growth as the key linear mechanism needed to sustain turbulence at R ​ e τ = 180 Re_{\tau}=180 .

title: On the Pre- and Promonoidal Structure of Spacetime
creator: James Hefford, Aleks Kissinger
description: Abstract The notion of a joint system, as captured by the monoidal (a.k.a. tensor) product, is fundamental to the compositional, process-theoretic approach to physical theories. Promonoidal categories generalise monoidal categories by replacing the functors normally used to form joint systems with profunctors.

title: On the equivalence of the BMO-norm of divergence-free vector fields and norm of related paracommutators
creator: M. N. Demchenko
description: Abstract We establish an estimate of the BMO-norm of a divergence-free vector field in ℝ 3 {\mathbb{R}}^{3} in terms of the operator norm of an associated paracommutator. The latter is essentially a Ψ \Psi DO, whose symbol depends linearly on the vector field. Together with the result of P. Auscher and M.

title: SafeBench: A Benchmarking Platform for Safety Evaluation of Autonomous Vehicles
creator: Chejian Xu, Wenhao Ding, Weijie Lyu, Zuxin Liu, Shuai Wang, Yihan He, Hanjiang Hu, Ding Zhao, Bo Li
description: Abstract As shown by recent studies, machine intelligence-enabled systems are vulnerable to test cases resulting from either adversarial manipulation or natural distribution shifts. This has raised great concerns about deploying machine learning algorithms for real-world applications, especially in safety-critical domains such as autonomous driving (AD).

title: Hydrodynamics of charged two-dimensional Dirac systems I: thermo-electric transport
creator: Kitinan Pongsangangan, T. Ludwig, H.T.C. Stoof, Lars Fritz
description: Abstract In this paper we study thermo-electric transport in interacting two-dimensional Dirac-type systems using a phenomenological Boltzmann approach. We consider a setup that can accommodate electrons, holes, and collective modes. In the first part of the paper we consider the electron-hole hydrodynamics, a model that is popular in the context of graphene, and its transport properties.
